and call upon me in the day of trouble;
I will rescue you, and you shall glorify me.”

But to the wicked man God says:
“What business have you reciting my statutes
or taking my covenant into your mouth?

For you loathe instruction
and fling my words behind your back.

When you see a thief, you go along with him,
and with adulterers you take your share.

Your mouth you let loose for evil,
and your tongue weaves deceit.

You sit and speak against your brother;
you slander your own mother’s son.

“Think about this, you who forget God,
or I will rip you to pieces, with no one to rescue you!

notes.text: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed over the temple singers (1 Chronicles 15:17; 16:5; 25:1), and the name came to be borne by a guild of singers descended from him (Ezra 2:41). Psalms 50 and 73–83 bear his name.
Hebrew ’el ’elohim YHWH, three names of God set side by side, as in Joshua 22:22.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba.{a}

verses.text:
Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity
and make me clean from my sin!

For I know my transgressions,
and my sin is before me at all times.

Behold, in iniquity I was brought forth,
and in sin my mother conceived me.

Behold, you take pleasure in truth in the inner being,
and in the secret place you teach me wisdom.

Cleanse me with hyssop,{c} and I shall be clean;
wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

Let me hear gladness and joy;
let the bones you have crushed rejoice.

Turn your face away from my sins,
and wipe out all my iniquities.

Create a clean heart in me, O God,
and make a steadfast spirit new within me.

Do not thrust me from your presence,
and do not remove your Holy Spirit from me.

Return to me the joy of your salvation,
and hold me up with a willing spirit.

Then I will teach transgressors your ways,
and sinners will turn back to you.

Rescue me from bloodguilt, O God,
O God of my salvation,
and my tongue will sing for joy of your righteousness.

Lord, open my lips,
and my mouth will declare your praise.

You take no pleasure in sacrifice, or I would offer one;
a burnt offering does not please you.

The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;
a broken and crushed heart, O God, you will not despise.

In your good pleasure do good to Zion;
build up the walls of Jerusalem.

notes.text: See 2 Samuel 11–12. In Hebrew the title is counted as verses 1–2, so Hebrew verse numbers in this psalm are two higher than the English.
Quoted from the Septuagint in Romans 3:4, “that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.”
Hyssop, a small bushy plant, was used to sprinkle water and blood in rites of cleansing (Exodus 12:22; Leviticus 14:4–7; Numbers 19:18).

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.”{a}

verses.text:
Why do you glory in evil, O mighty man?
The covenant love of God endures all the day.{b}

Your tongue plots destruction,
like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.

You love evil more than good,
lying more than speaking what is right.
Selah

You love all words that devour,
O tongue of deceit.

God will likewise break you down forever;
he will snatch you and tear you from your tent
and root you out of the land of the living.
Selah

The righteous shall see it and fear,
and they shall laugh at him, saying,

But as for me, I am like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God;
I trust in the covenant love of God forever and ever.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 21:1–9; 22:9–19. In Hebrew the title is counted as verses 1–2.
Hebrew “the khesed of God is all the day.” The Syriac has “against the godly.”
Or “in his desire,” with the Syriac and Targum.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to Mahalath.{a} A Maskil of David.

verses.text:
God looks down from heaven
upon the children of man,
to see if there is any who understands,
who seeks after God.

Have they no knowledge, those workers of iniquity,
who devour my people as they devour bread,
and do not call upon God?

notes.text: Hebrew mahalat, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps the name of a tune or a term meaning “sickness” or “sorrow” (also in Psalm 88). This psalm is nearly identical to Psalm 14, but uses “God” (Elohim) where Psalm 14 has “Yahweh,” and verse 5 differs.
Compare Psalm 14:5–6, which reads differently.
Or “brings back the captivity of his people,” as in Psalm 14:7.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: with stringed instruments.{a} A Maskil of David, when the men of Ziph came and told Saul, “David is hiding with us, is he not?”

verses.text:
O God, by your name save me,
and by your power defend my cause.

O God, hear my prayer;
give ear to the words of my mouth.

For strangers{b} have stood up against me,
and violent men hunt for my life;
they have not set God in front of them.
Selah

Behold, God is my helper;
the Lord is the upholder of my life.{c}

He will turn back the evil on my enemies;{d}
by your truth make an end of them.

With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you;
I will give thanks to your name, Yahweh, for it is good.

For he has delivered me out of all distress,
and my eye has gazed upon my enemies.

notes.text: Hebrew neginot. See 1 Samuel 23:19; 26:1. In Hebrew the title is counted as verses 1–2.
Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Targum have “arrogant men,” as in Psalm 86:14.
Or “the Lord is among those who uphold my life.”
So the qere; the ketiv has “The evil will return to my enemies.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.

verses.text:
Listen to my prayer, O God,
and do not hide yourself from my plea!

Attend to me and answer me;
I am restless in my complaint, and I moan,

at the shouting of the enemy,
at the oppression by the wicked;
for they drop disaster on me
and attack me in rage.

My heart writhes within me;
the terrors of death have fallen upon me.

Fear and trembling come into me,
and horror has wrapped me round.

And I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove!
I would fly off and find rest.

Yes, I would wander far off
and stay in the desert.
Selah

I would make haste to my place of escape
from the raging wind and tempest.”

Swallow them up, Lord; split their speech;{a}
for I have seen violence and quarreling in the city.

Day and night they make the rounds on its walls,
and wickedness and trouble are in its midst;

ruin is within it;
oppression and fraud never leave its marketplace.

But it was you, a man of my own rank,
my close friend, whom I knew well.

We used to share sweet counsel together;
we walked with the throng in the house of God.

But I call to God,
and Yahweh will save me.

Evening and morning and noon
I complain and groan,
and he hears my voice.

God will hear and answer them,
he who sits enthroned of old,
Selah
those who have no changes
and who have no fear of God.

That man{c} put forth his hands against those at peace with him;
he broke his covenant.

His talk was smoother than cream,
but his heart was set on war;
his words were gentler than oil,
but they were swords out of their sheaths.

Throw your burden{d} on Yahweh, and he will sustain you;
he will never let the righteous be shaken.

But you, O God, will bring them down
into the pit of destruction;
men of blood and deceit
shall not live out half their days.
But I will trust in you.

notes.text: Compare Genesis 11:1–9.
Compare Numbers 16:30–33. “Let death come upon them by surprise” follows the qere; the ketiv has “Desolations be upon them.”
Hebrew “He.”
Or “what he has given you.” Compare 1 Peter 5:7.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to “The Silent Dove of Distant Places.”{a} A Miktam{b} of David, when the Philistines laid hold of him at Gath.

verses.text:
Have mercy on me, O God, for man would swallow me up;
the fighter presses me all the day.

My watchful foes would swallow me up all day long,
for many are those who war against me proudly.{c}

On the day I am afraid,
I put my trust in you.

All day long they twist my words;
all their plans are against me for evil.

Because of their iniquity, cast them out;{d}
in anger bring down the peoples, O God!

In God, whose promise I praise,
in Yahweh, whose promise I praise,

I have put my trust in God and will not be afraid.
What can a mere human do to me?

Your vows are upon me, O God;
I will render thank offerings to you.

For you have delivered my soul from death,
yes, my feet from stumbling,
that I may walk before God
in the light of the living.

notes.text: Hebrew yonat ’elem rehoqim, probably the name of a tune. See 1 Samuel 21:10–15.
Hebrew miktam, a term of uncertain meaning (also in the titles of Psalms 16 and 57–60).
Or “O Most High.”
Hebrew “For iniquity, deliverance for them?” The text is difficult.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: “Do Not Destroy.”{a} A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.

verses.text:
Pity me, God, pity me,
for my soul runs to you for safety;
I will find safety under your wings
until the disaster is over.

I cry out to God Most High,
to God who brings about his purpose for me.

He will send from heaven and save me;
he will shame the one who tramples on me.
Selah
God will send out his covenant love and his faithfulness!

My soul is in the midst of lions;
I lie down among those who breathe fire,
the children of man, whose teeth are spears and arrows,
whose tongues are sharp swords.

Be exalted, O God, above the heavens!
Let your glory be over all the earth!

My heart is firm, O God, my heart is firm!
I will sing and make music!

I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the peoples;
I will sing your praise among the nations.

For your covenant love is great, reaching to the heavens,
and your faithfulness to the clouds.

Be exalted, O God, above the heavens!
Let your glory be over all the earth!

notes.text: Hebrew ’al-tashhet, probably the name of a tune (also in the titles of Psalms 58, 59, and 75). See 1 Samuel 22:1; 24:3. Verses 7–11 appear again as Psalm 108:1–5.
That is, my soul, or my whole being.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David.

verses.text:
Do you indeed speak righteousness, you gods?{a}
Do you judge uprightly the sons of men?

No, in your hearts you devise wrongs;
on the earth your hands deal out violence.

The wicked go astray from the womb;
liars, they wander off from birth.

Their poison is like a snake’s poison,
like a deaf adder that stops up its ear,

so that it does not hear the voice of the charmers,
of the cunning enchanter.

O God, shatter their teeth in their mouth;
break out the jaw teeth of the young lions, Yahweh!

Let them flow away like waters that run off;
when he bends his bow, let his arrows be blunted.{b}

Let them be like the snail that melts away as it goes,
like a stillborn child that never sees the sun.

Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns,
whether green or burning, may he sweep them away!{c}

The righteous will rejoice when he sees vengeance;
he will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.

And mankind will say, “Surely there is a reward for the righteous;
surely there is a God who judges on earth.”

notes.text: Hebrew ’elem, “silence,” probably to be read ’elim, “gods,” that is, rulers or heavenly beings who are set over the nations (compare Psalm 82).
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent and they guarded the house to put him to death.{a}

verses.text:
Rescue me from my enemies, O my God;
set me high above those who rise against me;

rescue me from those who work iniquity,
and save me from men of blood.

for no guilt of mine they run and make ready.
Rouse yourself to meet me, and see!

You, Yahweh, God of Armies, God of Israel,
arise to visit all the nations;
show no mercy to any wicked traitors.
Selah

Look, they spew out with their mouths,
with swords in their lips—
“for who,” they say, “will hear us?”

But you, Yahweh, will laugh at them;
you will mock all the nations.

O my Strength, I will keep watch for you,{b}
for God is my high tower.

My God, who is faithful to me, will come to meet me;{c}
God will let me see my enemies defeated.

For the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips,
may they be trapped in their pride,
and for the curses and falsehood they tell.

Finish them off in wrath; finish them, so they are gone,
and let them know to the ends of the earth
that God is ruler in Jacob.
Selah

They wander up and down for food,
and if they are not filled, they stay all night.{d}

But I will sing about your power;
in the morning I will joyfully sing about your steadfast love.
You have been my stronghold
and my place of safety when I was in trouble.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 19:11–17.
So some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and the Targum (compare verse 17); most Hebrew manuscripts have “his strength.”
So the qere; the ketiv has “The God of my covenant love.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint and Vulgate read “and grumble.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: set to “Lily of the Testimony.”{a} A Miktam of David, to be taught, when he made war with Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab came back and slew 12,000 of Edom in the Valley of Salt.{b}

verses.text:
O God, you have rejected us and broken through our defenses;{c}
you have been angry. Restore us again!

You have made the land quake; you have split it open;
mend its cracks, for it totters.

You have shown your people harsh things;
you have made us drink a wine of reeling.

That your beloved ones may be delivered,
save with your right hand and answer us!{e}

Who will bring me into the strong city?
Who will guide me to Edom?

Is it not you, O God, who have cast us off?
You, O God, who no longer go out with our armies?

Give us help against the adversary,
for vain is the deliverance of man!

With God we shall do valiantly;
it is he who will trample our adversaries.

notes.text: Hebrew shushan ‘edut, probably the name of a tune. In Hebrew the title is counted as verses 1–2.
See 2 Samuel 8:3–14 and 1 Chronicles 18:3–13, where Abishai is credited with 18,000. Verses 5–12 appear again as Psalm 108:6–13.
Hebrew “broken us.”
Or “that they may flee to it from the bow.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv has “answer me.”
Or “in his sanctuary.”
A gesture of taking possession (compare Ruth 4:7).

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on stringed instruments. Of David.

verses.text:
Hear my crying, O God;
give heed to my prayer.

From the far end of the earth I call to you
as my heart grows faint.
Lead me to a rock too high for me,

for you have been my shelter,
a strong tower against the enemy.

Let me be a guest in your tent forever!
Let me shelter under the cover of your wings!
Selah

For you, O God, have listened to my vows;
you have given me the heritage of those who fear your name.

Add days to the days of the king;
may his years be as generation upon generation!

May he sit enthroned before God forever;
appoint covenant love and faithfulness to guard him!

So will I sing praise to your name forever,
as I fulfill my vows day after day.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Truly my soul is silent{a} before God alone;
from him comes my salvation.

He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my high fortress; I shall not be greatly shaken.

How long will you assault a man,
all of you, to batter him down,
as you would a leaning wall, a tottering fence?

They only plan to thrust him from his high place;
they take pleasure in falsehood.
With their mouths they bless,
but inwardly they curse.
Selah

My soul, be silent before God alone,
for my hope comes from him.

He alone is my rock and my salvation,
my high fortress; I shall not be shaken.

Upon God rests my salvation and my glory;
my rock of strength, my refuge, is in God.

and to you, Lord, belongs covenant love.
For you repay each one according to his deeds.{b}

notes.text: Or “waits in stillness.” The word recurs in verse 5.
Compare Matthew 16:27; Romans 2:6.

chapters.title: A psalm of David, while he was in the desert of Judah.{a}

verses.text:
Thus I have gazed on you in the holy place,
to see your might and your glory.

Because your covenant love is better than life,
my lips shall praise you.

Therefore I will bless you all my life;
I will raise my hands in your name.

My soul shall be satisfied as with fat and rich food,
and my mouth shall praise you with songs of joy on my lips,

when I call you to mind upon my bed
and think on you through the watches of the night;

for you have been my help,
and in the shadow of your wings I sing for joy.

My soul holds fast to you;
your right hand keeps hold of me.

But those who hunt my life to ruin it
will go down to the lowest parts of the earth;

they shall be given over to the power of the sword;
they shall be a portion for jackals.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 22:5; 23:14; 2 Samuel 15:23–28.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
God, listen to me as I lament;
protect my life from the terror of the enemy.

Hide me from the secret plotting of evildoers,
from the throng of those who do iniquity,

who whet their tongue like a sword
and fit their arrows, bitter words, to the bow,

to shoot in secret at the upright;
all at once they shoot at him and are not afraid.

They search out injustices, saying,
“We have perfected a well-planned scheme!”
For the inward mind and heart of a man are deep.

But God will shoot his arrow at them;
suddenly they will be wounded.

They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them;
all who see them will shake their heads.

The righteous one will rejoice in Yahweh
and take refuge in him.
All the upright in heart will glory!

notes.text: So the Hebrew; some manuscripts and the Syriac have “see us.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A psalm of David. A song.

verses.text:
Praise waits for you,{a} O God, in Zion,
and to you shall vows be paid.

You who listen to prayer,
all flesh will come before you.

Deeds of iniquity overpower me;
our transgressions you cover over.

Happy is the man whom you choose and draw near
to live in your courts!
We will be filled with the goodness of your house,
your holy temple.

You answer us with fearsome acts of justice,
God our savior,
the hope of everyone across the earth
and of those on distant seas;

who by his strength set the mountains firm,
being girded with might;

who stills the roaring of the seas,
the roaring of their waves,
and the tumult of the peoples,

Those who dwell at the earth’s far edges stand in awe of your wonders;
the gateways of morning and evening you make to sing for joy.

You drench its furrows,
you level its ridges,
you soften it with showers,
and you bless its growth.

You crown the year with your goodness;
your tracks overflow with abundance.{b}

The wilderness grasslands drip with plenty,
and the hills are wrapped in rejoicing;

notes.text: So the Hebrew vowels (“silence is praise to you”); the Septuagint has “Praise is fitting for you.”
Hebrew “drip with fatness,” the image of the wheel ruts of God’s chariot spilling plenty as it passes.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. A song. A psalm.

verses.text: Raise a shout to God, all the earth!

Sing out the glory of his name;
make his praise glorious!

Say to God, “How fearsome are your works!
Because of your great strength your enemies feign obedience to you.

Come and look at the works of God,
fearsome in his dealings with the children of man.

O peoples, bless our God;
make the voice of his praise heard,

who keeps our soul alive
and has not let our feet be shaken.

For you, O God, have tested us;
you have refined us as silver is refined.

You led us into the snare;
you put heavy affliction on our loins;

I will come into your house with burnt offerings;
I will pay you my vows,

the vows my lips spoke
and my mouth promised when I was in distress.

Burnt offerings of fatlings I will bring you,
with the sweet smoke of rams;
bulls with goats I will prepare.
Selah

Come and listen, all you who fear God,
and I will tell what he has done for my soul.

I called out to him with my mouth,
and his praise was under my tongue.

If I had cherished iniquity in my heart,
the Lord would not have listened.

But God has indeed heard me;
he has paid attention to my prayer.

Blessed be God,
who has not turned away my prayer
or withdrawn his covenant love from me!

notes.text: Compare Exodus 14:21–22; Joshua 3:14–17.
So the qere; the ketiv has a different form of the verb.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint, Syriac, and Jerome have “to a place of refreshment.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

verses.text:
so that your way may become known on earth,
your saving power among all the nations.

Let the peoples give thanks to you, O God;
let all the peoples give thanks to you!

Let the nations be glad and sing aloud,
for you will judge the peoples in uprightness
and guide the nations on the earth.
Selah

Let the peoples give thanks to you, O God;
let all the peoples give thanks to you!

The earth has yielded its harvest;
God, our God, blesses us.

God will bless us,
and all the ends of the earth will fear him.

notes.text: Echoing the priestly blessing of Numbers 6:24–26.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David. A psalm. A song.

verses.text:
God rises up; his enemies scatter;
those who hate him run from his face.{a}

But let the righteous be glad and exult before God;
let them be jubilant with joy.

Father of the fatherless and defender of widows
is God in his holy dwelling.

O God, when you went out before your people,
when you strode through the wasteland,
Selah

You shed abroad a generous rain, O God;
your inheritance was weary, and you restored it.

Your company of creatures{e} settled there;
out of your bounty, O God, you made ready for the afflicted.

The Lord gives the word;
the women who bring the news are a great army:{f}

“Kings of armies flee, they flee!”
The woman who stays at home divides the plunder.

As Shaddai{h} scattered the kings in it,
it was snowing on Zalmon.{i}

A mountain of God is Bashan’s mountain;
a mountain of many summits is Bashan’s mountain!

Why do you look with envy, you many-peaked mountains,
on the mount that God desired for his dwelling?
Yes, Yahweh will dwell there forever.

God’s chariots number twenty thousand, thousands repeated;
the Lord is in their midst; Sinai is in holiness.{j}

Blessed be the Lord, who carries us{l} day by day,
the God who is our salvation.
Selah

Our God is a God of saving acts,
and to Yahweh the Lord belong the ways out from death.

Surely God will crush the heads of his enemies,
the hairy crown of him who walks on in his guilt.

The Lord has said, “From Bashan I will bring back;
I will bring back from the deep places of the sea,

that you may strike your foot in blood,{m}
and the tongues of your dogs may have their share of the enemy.”

Your processions are seen, O God,
the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary:

singers in front, musicians last,
between them young women playing tambourines:

“In the great assemblies bless God,
bless Yahweh, you who are from Israel’s fountain!”

Your God has commanded your strength;{n}
show your strength, O God, you who have acted for us.

Because of your temple above Jerusalem,
kings will bring gifts to you.

Envoys will come from Egypt;
Cush{q} will hurry to stretch out her hands to God.

to him who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens;
see, he sends out his voice, a voice of power.

notes.text: Compare Numbers 10:35, the cry when the ark set out.
Or “extol him who rides on the clouds.” Hebrew ʿarabot, “desert plains”; compare verse 33.
Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh; compare Exodus 15:2.
Or “even Sinai quaked.” Compare Judges 5:4–5.
Hebrew khayyah, “living things,” perhaps here “your flock” or “your people.”
The Hebrew participle is feminine; compare Exodus 15:20; 1 Samuel 18:6.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; compare Judges 5:16.
Shaddai, traditionally “the Almighty.”
Zalmon is a hill near Shechem (Judges 9:48), or “it snowed in the darkness.” The verse is obscure.
Or “the Lord has come from Sinai into the holy place,” with a slight change to the Hebrew.
Ephesians 4:8 quotes this line in the form “gave gifts to men,” agreeing with the Aramaic Targum and the Syriac.
Or “who bears our burdens.”
So the Hebrew (“crush”); the Septuagint and Syriac have “dip your foot.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint, Syriac, and some Hebrew manuscripts have “Command your strength, O God.”
Probably Egypt, pictured as a crocodile or hippopotamus.
Or “until each one submits with bars of silver.” The Hebrew is very difficult.
The upper Nile region, south of Egypt.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to “Lilies.” Of David.

verses.text:
Rescue me, O God,
for the waters have reached my throat.{a}

I have sunk in deep mud,
and there is no foothold;
I have come into the depths of the waters,
and the flood sweeps over me.

I am weary from calling out; my throat is dry;
my eyes fail as I wait for my God.

You, O God, know my foolishness,
and my guilty deeds are not concealed from you.

For your sake I have endured insult;
disgrace has covered my face.

I have become a stranger to my brothers,
a foreigner to the sons of my mother.

Zeal for your house has eaten me up,{c}
and the scorn of those who scorn you has fallen on me.{d}

When I wept, with my soul in fasting,
that became a reproach against me.

When I made sackcloth my clothing,
I became a byword to them.

Those who sit at the gate talk about me,
and drunkards make songs about me.

But as for me, my prayer is to you, Yahweh,
at a time of favor.
O God, in the abundance of your covenant love,
answer me with your sure salvation.

Do not let the flood overwhelm me
or the deep swallow me up
or the pit shut its mouth on me.

Answer me, Yahweh, for your covenant love is good;
in the greatness of your compassion turn to me.

Do not hide your face from your servant,
for I am in distress; quickly answer me.

Come near to my soul and redeem it;
ransom me because of my enemies.

They put poison{e} in my food,
and for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.{f}

Let their table before them become a trap,
and for those at ease, a snare.{g}

Let their eyes grow dark so they cannot see,
and make their loins shake without ceasing.

Pour out your fury on them,
and let the heat of your anger catch them.

Let their camp become a ruin;
let no one live in their tents.{h}

For they persecute the one you have struck,
and they recount the pain of those you have wounded.

Add guilt to their guilt;
let them have no share in your righteousness.

Let them be blotted from the book of life;
let them not be written down with the righteous.

But I am lowly and in sorrow;
let your saving help, O God, set me on high.

I will praise the name of God in a song
and glorify him with thanksgiving.

This will please Yahweh better than an ox,
a young bull with horns and split hoofs.

The lowly have seen and rejoice;
you seekers of God, may your heart live.

For Yahweh listens to the needy
and does not scorn his own who are captive.

Let heaven and earth praise him,
the seas and everything that moves in them.

the children of his servants will inherit it,
and those who love his name will live there.

notes.text: Hebrew nephesh, here in its basic sense of “throat” or “neck.”
Quoted in John 15:25.
Quoted in John 2:17.
Quoted in Romans 15:3.
Hebrew rosh, a bitter, poisonous plant; the Septuagint has “gall.”
Compare Matthew 27:34, 48; John 19:28–29.
Or “and their peace offerings a snare.” Verses 22–23 are quoted in Romans 11:9–10, following the Septuagint.
Quoted in Acts 1:20.

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of David. For a memorial offering.{a}

verses.text:
O God, hurry to rescue me!
Yahweh, hurry to help me!

Let them be shamed and put to confusion
who seek after my life!
Let them be driven back and humiliated
who take pleasure in my hurt!

Let those who cry, “Aha, aha!”
be turned back as the wage of their shame.

May all who seek you
be glad and rejoice in you!
May those who love your salvation
always say, “God is great!”

notes.text: Compare the title of Psalm 38. This psalm closely matches Psalm 40:13–17. In Hebrew numbering the title is verse 1, so the Hebrew has six verses.

verses.text:
In you, Yahweh, I have found refuge;{a}
let me never be shamed.

By your righteousness rescue me and set me free;
bend your ear to me and save me.

Be a rock of dwelling for me,
where I may always come;
you have given the command to save me,
for you are my rock and my stronghold.

My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked,
from the grasp of the unjust and the ruthless.

For you are my hope, Lord Yahweh,
my confidence from my youth.

I have become like a portent to many,
but you are my strong refuge.

My mouth is full of your praise,
of your splendor all day long.

Do not throw me away when I am old;
do not abandon me as my strength fails.

For my enemies talk against me;
those who watch for my life plot together,

O God, do not stay far from me;
my God, hurry to my help!{c}

But I will always hope
and will praise you more and more.

My mouth will tell of your righteousness,
of your saving deeds all the day,
though their number is past my knowing.

I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord Yahweh;
I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.

O God, you have taught me since my youth,
and until now I proclaim your wonders.

And now, when I am old and gray-haired,
O God, do not forsake me,
till I declare your arm to this generation,
your power to everyone yet to come.

You who have shown me{d} many bitter troubles
will make me live once more;
from the deeps of the earth
you will raise me up again.

You will increase my greatness
and turn again to comfort me.

I also will praise you with the harp
for your faithfulness, my God;
I will make music to you with the lyre,
O Holy One of Israel.

My lips will shout for joy when I make music to you,
and my soul, which you have redeemed.

My tongue will also tell of your righteousness all day,
for those who tried to hurt me
have been shamed and humiliated.

notes.text: This psalm has no title. Verses 1–3 closely follow Psalm 31:1–3.
Or “who cut the cord,” an uncertain Hebrew word.
So the qere; the ketiv has a variant spelling.
So the qere throughout this verse; the ketiv has “us.”

chapters.title: Of Solomon.{a}

verses.text:
God, give your decisions to the king,
and your righteousness to the king’s son.

May he judge your people with righteousness
and your afflicted ones with justice.

Let the mountains bear peace for the people,
and the hills, through righteousness.

May he do justice for the lowly among the people,
save the sons of the needy,
and break the oppressor in pieces.

May they fear you{b} while the sun endures,
and as long as the moon, through all generations.

May he be like rain falling on the mown field,
like showers that water the land.

Let the righteous flourish in his days,
and let there be much peace until the moon is gone.

May he rule from sea to sea,
and from the River{c} to the ends of the earth.

May the desert dwellers bow down before him,
and his enemies lick the dust.

May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands
render tribute;
may the kings of Sheba and Seba
bring gifts.

May all kings fall down before him,
all nations serve him.

For he rescues the needy who cry out,
the afflicted, and the one who has no helper.

He will spare the poor and needy one
and will save the souls of the needy.

From oppression and violence he redeems their lives,
and their blood is precious in his eyes.

Blessed be Yahweh God, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonders.
The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.{g}

notes.text: Or “For Solomon.” A prayer for the king, closing Book Two.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “May he endure.”
The Euphrates.
So the qere; the ketiv has a variant form, “sprout.”
Compare Genesis 12:3; 22:18.
Verses 18–19 are the doxology that closes Book Two of the Psalms; compare 41:13; 89:52; 106:48; and Psalm 150.
An editorial note closing an earlier collection of David’s psalms; some psalms of David still follow (for example, 86, 101, 103, 108–110, 138–145).

chapters.heading: Book Three (Psalms 73–89)
chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.{a}

verses.text:
Surely God is good to Israel,
to those who are pure of heart.

But as for me, my feet had nearly turned aside;{b}
my steps had all but slid away.

For I grew jealous of the boastful
when I watched the wicked prosper.

For they have no pangs until their death;{c}
their bodies are sleek and fat.

They have no share in the toil of mortals;
they are not struck down as other people are.

So pride is their necklace;
violence wraps them like a robe.

Their eyes bulge out from fatness;{d}
the fancies of their hearts overflow.

They jeer and speak with malice;
from on high they talk of oppression.

They have set their mouths against the heavens,
and their tongues strut across the earth.

Therefore his people turn back to them,{e}
and they drain waters in full measure.{f}

And they say, “How does God know?
Is there knowledge with the Most High?”

Look at them: these are the wicked,
always at ease; they pile up wealth.

In vain, then, I have kept my heart pure
and bathed my hands in innocence.

For I have been struck all day long,
and my rebuke comes every morning.

If I had said, “I will talk like this,”
I would have betrayed the generation of your children.

But when I set myself to understand this,
it was a weary task in my eyes,

until I entered the sanctuaries of God;{g}
then I perceived their end.

Truly you place them on slippery ground;
you hurl them down to ruin.

How suddenly they become a desolation,
swept away entirely by terrors!

Like a dream after one wakes, Lord,
so when you rouse yourself you will despise their phantoms.

When my heart was soured
and I was stabbed in my inward parts,{h}

I was stupid and did not understand;
I was a brute beast toward you.

Still, I am with you continually;
you hold me by my right hand.

You will lead me with your counsel,
and afterward you will receive me with glory.{i}

Whom do I have in heaven but you?
And besides you I want nothing on earth.

My flesh and my heart may waste away,
but God is the rock{j} of my heart and my portion forever.

For look: those far from you will be lost;
you silence all who go whoring away from you.

notes.text: Book Three of the Psalms begins here; it closes with the doxology at 89:52. Psalms 73–83 form a collection attributed to Asaph, a Levite singer appointed by David (1 Chronicles 15:17–19; 16:4–7; 25:1–2); compare Psalm 50. Psalms 84–85 and 87–88 belong to the sons of Korah.
So the qere for both verbs; the ketiv has variant forms.
Or, dividing the Hebrew differently, “they have no pangs; sound and fat is their body.”
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint and Syriac have “their iniquity comes out from fatness.”
So the ketiv; the qere has “he brings back his people here.”
The meaning of the Hebrew in this verse is uncertain.
Or “the holy things of God.”
Hebrew “kidneys,” the seat of the emotions.
Or “take me to glory.”
Hebrew tsur, “rock.”

chapters.title: A Maskil of Asaph.{a}

verses.text:
Why, O God, have you rejected us forever?
Why does your anger smoke against the sheep you pasture?

Remember your assembly, which you acquired long ago,
the tribe of your inheritance, which you redeemed,
Mount Zion, where you have made your dwelling.

Lift your steps toward the endless ruins,
everything the enemy has wrecked in the holy place.

Your foes have roared in the middle of your meeting place;
they have set up their own banners as signs.

They looked like men swinging axes
upward into a thicket of trees.{b}

And now all its carved panels{c}
they smash with hatchet and hammers.

They have set your sanctuary on fire;
they have profaned the dwelling of your name, bringing it to the ground.

They said in their hearts, “Let us crush them altogether”;
they burned every meeting place of God in the land.

How long, O God, will the foe taunt?
Is the enemy to scorn your name forever?

Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand?
Take it out of the fold of your garment{d} and finish them off!

Yet God has been my King since long ago,
bringing rescue across the land.

You split the sea by your might;
you shattered the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.

You crushed the heads of Leviathan;{e}
you gave him as food to the people of the wilderness.{f}

You split open fountain and stream;
you made the ever-running rivers dry.

The day belongs to you, and the night is yours as well;
you established the moon{g} and the sun.

You fixed all the boundaries of the earth;
summer and winter you formed.

Remember this, Yahweh: the enemy taunts,
and a foolish people scorns your name.

Do not hand over your turtledove’s soul to the wild beast;
do not forget forever the life of your poor.

Look to the covenant,
for the dark corners of the land are full of the haunts of violence.

Let not the downtrodden turn back in disgrace;
let the poor and needy praise your name.

Rise up, O God, argue your own case;
remember how the fool taunts you all day long.

Do not forget the clamor of your adversaries,
the din of those rising up against you, ascending continually.

notes.text: A lament over the destruction of the sanctuary, most likely by the Babylonians in 587 BC (2 Kings 25:8–9). On Maskil, see Psalm 32.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv has a variant spelling.
So the qere; the ketiv has “your statute.”
A many-headed sea serpent, a picture of chaos; compare Job 41; Isaiah 27:1.
Or “to the creatures of the desert.”
Hebrew “the light,” probably the moon.

chapters.title: To the director: set to “Destroy Not.” A psalm of Asaph; a song.

verses.text:
“When I seize the appointed time,
I myself will judge with equity.

When the earth and all who live on it reel,
it is I who keep its pillars steady.
Selah

To the arrogant I say, ‘Stop your boasting,’
and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up the horn;{b}

do not lift your horn on high,
or speak with an arrogant neck.’”

For promotion comes not from the east or the west
or from the wilderness;{c}

but it is God who judges,
bringing one low and lifting another up.

But I will declare it forever;
I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

“All the horns of the wicked I will cut off,
but the horns of the righteous will be raised high.”

notes.text: So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “we will call on your name.”
The horn is a picture of strength and pride; so also in verses 5 and 10.
Or “not from the desert of the mountains.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

verses.text:
In Judah God is known;
his name is great in Israel.

His shelter{a} has been set up in Salem,{b}
his lair in Zion.

There he shattered the fiery shafts of the bow,
the shield and sword and battle gear.
Selah

Radiant are you,
more majestic than the mountains of prey.{c}

At your rebuke, O God of Jacob,
both chariot and horse lay stunned.

You—you are to be feared!
Who can stand before you once your anger is roused?

From the heavens you made your judgment heard;
the earth was afraid and fell silent

when God rose up to judge,
to save all the humble of the earth.
Selah

Surely the wrath of man will praise you;
with the remnant of wrath you will gird yourself.{d}

Make vows to Yahweh your God and keep them;
let all around him bring tribute to the One to be feared,

who cuts short the breath of princes,
who is fearsome to the kings of the earth.

notes.text: Or “his booth,” the image of a lion’s thicket.
An old name for Jerusalem; compare Genesis 14:18.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint has “the everlasting mountains.”
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to Jeduthun.{a} Of Asaph. A psalm.

verses.text:
My voice goes up to God, and I cry out;
my voice goes up to God, and he will listen to me.

You hold my eyelids open;
I am so troubled I cannot speak.

I consider the days long past,
the years of ages gone by.

“Will the Lord cast off for all time
and be favorable no more?

Has his covenant love come to an end for all time?
Is his promise at an end for all generations?

Has God forgotten to be gracious?
Has he in anger shut off his compassion?”
Selah

Then I said, “What hurts me most
is that the right hand of the Most High is different now.”{b}

I will call to mind the deeds of Yah;{c}
yes, I will remember your wonders of old.

I will think over everything you have done
and reflect on your mighty deeds.

O God, your way is in holiness.
What god is great like our God?

You are the God who works wonders;
you have made your strength known among the peoples.

By your arm you have ransomed your people,
Jacob’s sons and Joseph’s.
Selah

Your road was in the sea,
your paths in the mighty waters,
and your tracks could not be known.

You led your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has “Jeduthun” spelled differently. Compare Psalm 39 and 62.
Or “I will appeal to the years of the right hand of the Most High.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
So the qere (“I will make mention of the deeds of Yah”); Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh.

chapters.title: A Maskil of Asaph.{a}

verses.text:
My people, hear my instruction;{b}
listen closely to what I say.

I will open my mouth in a parable;
I will pour out riddles from long ago,{c}

things we have heard and known,
which our fathers have recounted to us.

We will not hide them from their descendants
but will tell the next generation
about the praiseworthy acts of Yahweh, his power,
and the wonders he has performed.

He set up a testimony in Jacob
and placed a law in Israel,
which he commanded our fathers
to teach to their children,

so that a later generation might know them,
children not yet born,
and rise up and recount them to their own children,

and that they should not be like their fathers,
a generation stubborn and defiant,
a generation whose heart was not steady,
whose spirit was not faithful to God.

The men of Ephraim, armed archers,{d}
turned back on the day of battle.

They did not keep God’s covenant
and would not walk in his law.

They let his deeds slip from memory,
and the marvels he had let them see.

In the sight of their fathers he did marvels
in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.{e}

He split the sea and let them pass through;
he made the waters stand up like a heap.

By day he led them with a cloud,
and all night long with the light of fire.

He split rocks in the wilderness
and gave them drink as from the great deep.

He brought streams out of the crag
and made waters flow down like rivers.

Yet they went on sinning still more against him,
defying the Most High in the desert.

They put God to the test in their hearts
by demanding the food they craved.

They spoke against God, saying,
“Can God lay out a table in the wilderness?

True, he struck the rock and waters gushed
and torrents overflowed;
but can he also give bread
or supply meat for his people?”

because they did not believe in God
or trust his power to save.

Yet he gave orders to the skies above
and opened the doors of heaven;

he rained manna on them to eat
and gave them the grain of heaven.

Mortals ate the bread of the mighty;{f}
he sent them food in abundance.

He roused the east wind across the sky
and guided the south wind by his might;

He showered flesh on them like dust,
and birds on the wing like sea sand;

he let them fall in the middle of their camp,
all around their dwellings.

So they ate and were thoroughly filled,
for he gave them what they craved.

They had not yet turned from their lust;
their food was still in their mouths

In spite of all this they sinned again;
they did not believe in his wonders.

So he ended their days like a breath,
and their years in sudden terror.

Whenever he killed some, the rest would seek him;
they would turn back and search eagerly for God.

They remembered that God was their rock,
and God Most High their redeemer.

But they flattered him with their mouths
and lied to him with their tongues.

For their heart was not steadfast with him;
they kept no faith with his covenant.

Yet he, being compassionate,
covered over their guilt and did not destroy them;
again and again he held back his anger
and did not rouse all his wrath.

He remembered that they were only flesh,
a breath that passes and does not come back.

How often they defied him in the wilderness
and grieved him in the desert!

Again and again they put God to the test
and grieved{h} Israel’s Holy One.

They gave no thought to his hand,
to the day he redeemed them from the adversary,

when he set his signs in Egypt
and his marvels in the region of Zoan.

He turned their rivers to blood,
so they could not drink from their streams.

He sent among them mixed swarms that ate them up,
and frogs that brought them ruin.

He handed their harvest to the caterpillar
and the fruit of their work to the locust.

He killed their vines with hail
and their sycamore figs with frost.{i}

He handed over their cattle to the hail
and their herds to bolts of fire.

He let loose on them his burning anger,
fury, indignation, and distress,
a band of messengers of disaster.

He struck every firstborn son in Egypt,
the beginning of their vigor, in the tents of Ham.{j}

Then he brought out his people like sheep
and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

He led them in safety, and they were not afraid,
but the sea covered over their enemies.

He led them to the border of his holy place,
to this mountain, which his right hand acquired.

Yet they tested and defied God Most High
and did not keep his testimonies.

They turned away and were faithless like their fathers;
they swerved like a bow that cannot be trusted.

They angered him with their high places;
they stirred his jealousy with their carved idols.

When God heard, he was furious
and utterly rejected Israel.

He forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh,{k}
the tent he had pitched among men,

and gave up his strength{l} to captivity,
his splendor into the hand of the foe.

He gave his people over to the sword
and was furious with his inheritance.

Fire devoured their young men,
and no marriage song was sung for their maidens.

Their priests fell by the sword,
and their widows could not weep.{m}

Then the Lord awoke like one who had slept,
like a mighty man shouting from wine.

He beat his foes back;
he gave them lasting disgrace.

He refused Joseph’s tent
and did not select Ephraim’s tribe,

but he chose the tribe of Judah,
Mount Zion, which he loves.

He built his sanctuary like the heights,{n}
like the earth, which he founded forever.

He chose David his servant
and took him from the sheep pens;

from following the ewes with lambs he brought him
to be shepherd of Jacob his people,
and of Israel his heritage.

He shepherded them with integrity of heart
and led them with skillful hands.

notes.text: A long teaching psalm recounting Israel’s history from the exodus to David; compare Psalms 105 and 106.
Hebrew torah, “instruction.”
Quoted in Matthew 13:35.
Hebrew “armed ones, shooters of the bow.”
Tanis, a city in the eastern Nile delta.
Or “the bread of angels,” as in the Septuagint.
Compare Numbers 11:31–34.
Or “provoked” or “set limits for”; the meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Ham is a poetic name for Egypt (Genesis 10:6).
Compare 1 Samuel 4; Jeremiah 7:12–14.
The ark of the covenant; compare Psalm 132:8.
Compare 1 Samuel 4:11, 19–22.
Or “like the high heavens.”

chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.

verses.text:
They have left the corpses of your servants
as food for the birds of the sky,
the flesh of your faithful ones for the beasts of the land.

Their blood they have spilled like water
on every side of Jerusalem,
with no one to bury them.

We are a reproach to those who live near us,
a joke and a scorn to those all about us.

How long, Yahweh? Will you be angry forever?
Will your jealousy go on burning like fire?

Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you,
and on the realms that never call upon your name;

for they have eaten up Jacob
and laid his pasture waste.

Help us, God of our salvation,
for your name’s glory;
deliver us and cover our sins
because of your name.

Why should the nations say,
“Where is their God?”
Let the avenging of your servants’ shed blood
be made known among the nations before our eyes.

Pay back into the laps{c} of our neighbors sevenfold
the taunts with which they taunted you, Lord.

notes.text: Or “our former iniquities.”
Hebrew “the sons of death.”
Hebrew “bosom,” the fold of a garment used as a pocket.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: according to “Lilies.” A testimony. Of Asaph. A psalm.

verses.text:
Shepherd of Israel, give ear,
you who lead Joseph like a flock!
You who are enthroned upon the cherubim,{a} shine out

before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh!
Awaken your might
and come to save us!

Restore us, O God;
let your face shine, and we will be saved.{b}

Yahweh, God of Armies,
how long will you smolder at the prayer of your people?

You have fed them bread made of tears
and given them tears to drink by the measure.{c}

You make us a cause of strife to our neighbors,
and our enemies jeer among themselves.

God of Armies, restore us;
let your face shine, and we will be saved.

You brought a vine out of Egypt;
you drove out the nations and planted it.

You cleared the ground before it;
it struck deep roots and filled the land.

Its shade covered the mountains,
and its branches the mighty cedars.{d}

It stretched out its shoots as far as the Sea,
its tendrils to the River.{e}

Why have you torn down its walls,
so that all who pass along the road strip its fruit?

The boar from the forest gnaws it,
and whatever moves in the field feeds on it.

the stock{f} that your right hand planted,
and the son you made strong for yourself.

It is burned with fire, cut down;
may they perish at the rebuke of your face!

Let your hand rest on the man at your right,
on the human being you made strong for yourself.

Then we will not turn away from you;
give us life, and we will call on your name.

Yahweh, God of Armies, restore us;
let your face shine, and we will be saved.

notes.text: The winged figures over the ark of the covenant; compare Exodus 25:18–22.
This refrain recurs, growing fuller, in verses 7 and 19.
Hebrew shalish, “a third,” a measure of perhaps a third of an ephah.
Hebrew “the cedars of God.”
The Mediterranean and the Euphrates.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on the Gittith.{a} Of Asaph.

verses.text:
Shout for joy to God our strength;
raise a glad cry to the God of Jacob!

Lift up a song and strike the tambourine,
the sweet lyre together with the harp.

Blow the ram’s horn at the new moon,
at the full moon, on the day of our feast.{b}

For it is a statute for Israel,
an ordinance of the God of Jacob.

“I took the load off his shoulder;
his hands were freed from the basket.{e}

Listen, my people, and I will give you a warning—
Israel, if only you would pay attention to me!

You must not have any foreign god among you;
you must not worship a strange god.

I am Yahweh your God,
who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

“But my people did not heed my voice;
Israel would have none of me.

So I let them go in the stubbornness of their hearts,
to walk by their own schemes.

Oh, if my people would listen to me,
if Israel would walk in my ways,

how swiftly I would humble their enemies
and turn my hand against their foes!

Those who hate Yahweh would cringe before him,
and their doom{g} would last forever.

But he would feed you{h} with the best of the wheat,
and I would fill you with honey out of the rock.”

notes.text: See the title of Psalm 8.
Probably the Feast of Booths in the seventh month (Leviticus 23:24, 34).
Or “over.”
Or “I heard a language I did not know.”
The basket for carrying clay or bricks; compare Exodus 1:11–14.
Meribah means “quarreling”; compare Exodus 17:1–7; Numbers 20:1–13.
Hebrew “their time.”
Hebrew “him,” that is, Israel.

chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.

verses.text:
God stands in the divine council;{a}
in the midst of the gods he gives judgment:

“How long will you judge unjustly
and show favor to the wicked?
Selah

Give justice to the weak and the fatherless;
uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute.

Set free the weak and the poor;
snatch them from the grip of the wicked.”

“I said, ‘You are gods,
sons of the Most High, all of you;

Yet you will die as mortals die
and fall like one of the rulers.’”

Rise up, O God, and judge the earth,
because all the nations are your inheritance!

notes.text: Hebrew ʿadat-ʾel, “the assembly of God” or “of El.” The “gods” (elohim) of verses 1 and 6 are understood as the heavenly beings who were thought to rule the nations (compare Deuteronomy 32:8 in the Septuagint and Dead Sea Scrolls), or as human rulers and judges acting in God’s name. Jesus quotes verse 6 in John 10:34–36.

chapters.title: A song. A psalm of Asaph.

verses.text:
O God, do not stay silent;
do not hold back or be quiet, O God!

For look, your enemies are in an uproar;
those who hate you have raised their heads.

Against your people they plot cunningly;
they conspire against those you shelter.

They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation,
so that the name of Israel is remembered no more!”

For they plot together with one heart;
against you they make a covenant:

the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,

Gebal{a} and Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia with those who live in Tyre;

Do to them as you did to Midian,
as to Sisera and Jabin at the Wadi Kishon,{d}

They perished at En-dor;
they became manure for the soil.

Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,
all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

who said, “Let us seize for ourselves
the pastures of God.”

O my God, make them like a spinning wheel of thistle,{e}
like straw driven by the wind.

As fire burns up a forest,
as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,

so chase them with your tempest
and terrify them with your storm.

Cover their faces with disgrace,
so that they may seek your name, Yahweh.

Let them be shamed and dismayed forever;
let them be humiliated and perish,

that they may know that you alone, whose name is Yahweh,
are the Most High over all the earth.

notes.text: Probably Byblos on the Phoenician coast, or a region south of the Dead Sea.
Hebrew “arm.”
Moab and Ammon (Genesis 19:36–38).
Compare Judges 4–8.
Or “tumbleweed”; Hebrew galgal, “wheel.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader: on the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
How lovely are your dwelling places,
Yahweh of Armies!

My soul yearns, even wastes away,
for the courts of Yahweh;
my heart and my flesh cry out with joy
to the living God.

Even the sparrow has found a home,
and the swallow a nest for herself,
where she may set down her young—
at your altars, Yahweh of Armies,
my King and my God.

Happy are those who live in your house,
forever singing your praise!
Selah

Happy is the one whose strength is in you,
in whose heart are the highways to Zion.{a}

They walk on from strength to strength;
every one of them is seen before God in Zion.

Look on our shield, O God;{d}
regard the face of your anointed one!

For one day in your courts is better
than a thousand anywhere else.{e}
I would sooner stand at the threshold of the house of my God
than make my home in the tents of wickedness.

Yahweh of Armies,
happy is the person who trusts in you!

notes.text: Hebrew “the highways”; that is, the pilgrim roads to Jerusalem.
Or “the valley of weeping” or “of balsam trees.”
Or “pools,” with different vowels.
Or “O God our shield, look.” The “shield” is the king; compare 89:18.
Hebrew “than a thousand.”

chapters.title: For the choir leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh, you showed favor to your land;
you restored the fortunes{a} of Jacob.

You gathered up all your wrath;
you turned away from your blazing anger.

Turn us back again, God of our salvation,
and put an end to your displeasure with us.

Will you be angry with us forever?
Will you stretch out your anger to every generation?

Will you not give us life once more,
so that your people may rejoice in you?

Show us your covenant love, Yahweh,
and give us your salvation.

Surely his salvation is close to those who fear him,
that glory may make its home in our land.

Covenant love and faithfulness have met;
righteousness and peace have kissed.

Faithfulness sprouts up from the earth,
and righteousness gazes down from heaven.

Yes, Yahweh will give what is good,
and our land will give its harvest.

Righteousness will go ahead of him
and make his footsteps a road.{b}

notes.text: Or “brought back the captives.”
Or “and will set us on the way of his steps.”

chapters.title: A prayer of David.

verses.text:
Bend down your ear, Yahweh, and answer me,
for I am poor and in need.

Be gracious to me, Lord,
for to you I call all day long.

Bring joy to the soul of your servant,
for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.

For you, Lord, are good and forgiving,
rich in covenant love to all who call to you.

Hear my prayer, Yahweh;
listen to my plea for grace.

In the day of my trouble I call to you,
for you will answer me.

There is none like you among the gods, Lord,
and no works are like yours.

All the nations you have made will come
and bow down before you, Lord,
and they will give glory to your name.

For you are great and do wonders;
you alone are God.

I will thank you, Lord my God, with my whole heart,
and I will glorify your name forever.

For great is your covenant love toward me;
you have rescued my soul from the depths of Sheol.{b}

But you, Lord, are a merciful and kind God,
patient and full of steadfast love and truth.{c}

Give me a token of your favor,
and my haters will see it and be ashamed,
for you, Yahweh, are the one who has aided and consoled me.

notes.text: Hebrew khasid, “one devoted to covenant love.”
The realm of the dead.
Compare Exodus 34:6.

chapters.title: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.

verses.text: His foundation is on the holy mountains.{a}

Yahweh loves the gates of Zion
above all the dwellings of Jacob.

Glorious things are said of you,
O city of God.
Selah

“I will record Rahab{b} and Babylon
among those who know me;
look, Philistia and Tyre, with Cush—
‘This one was born there,’ they say.”

And of Zion it will be said,
“This one and that one were born in her,”
and the Most High himself will make her secure.

Yahweh records as he writes down the peoples,
“This one was born there.”
Selah

Singers and dancers alike will say,
“All my springs are in you.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of this brief psalm is compressed and in places obscure.
A poetic name for Egypt; compare 89:10; Isaiah 30:7.

chapters.title: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choir leader: according to Mahalath Leannoth.{a} A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.{b}

verses.text:
Yahweh, God of my salvation,
by day I cry out, and by night before you.

Let my prayer come into your presence;
turn your ear to my crying!

For my soul is sated with troubles,
and my life has drawn near to Sheol.

I am reckoned among those who go down to the pit;
I am like a man without strength,

cast loose among the dead,
like the slain who lie in the grave,
whom you remember no longer,
for they are cut off from your hand.

You have put me in the lowest pit,
in dark places, in the depths.

Your fury lies heavy on me,
and you overwhelm me with all your breakers.
Selah

Will you show wonders to the dead?
Will the departed{c} stand up and praise you?
Selah

Is your covenant love told in the grave,
or your faithfulness in Abaddon?{d}

Are your wonders known in the darkness,
or your righteousness in the land of forgetting?

But I cry to you, Yahweh, for help;
in the morning my prayer comes before you.

Yahweh, why do you reject me?
Why do you keep your face hidden from me?

I have been afflicted and close to death since my youth;
I bear your terrors; I am helpless.{e}

Your burning anger has swept over me;
your terrors have destroyed me.

They surround me like water all day;
they close in on me together.

You have taken lover and companion far from me;
my closest friend is darkness.{f}

notes.text: Perhaps “on sickness, for affliction,” or the name of a tune; the meaning is uncertain.
Compare 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chronicles 2:6; 15:19. This is the darkest of the laments; it ends without any word of hope.
Hebrew rephaim, the dead in the underworld.
“Destruction,” a name for the place of the dead.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Or “my companions are in darkness.”

chapters.title: A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.{a}

verses.text:
I will sing of the covenant love of Yahweh forever;
with my mouth I will make your faithfulness known to every generation.

For I said, “Covenant love is built up forever;
in the heavens you have fixed your faithfulness.”

“I have cut a covenant with my chosen one;
I have sworn to David my servant:

‘I will make your offspring secure forever
and build up your throne for all generations.’”
Selah

The heavens praise your wonders, Yahweh,
and your faithfulness in the gathering of the holy ones.

For who in the skies can be ranked with Yahweh?
Who among the sons of the gods{b} is like Yahweh,

a God feared in the assembly of the holy ones,
more awesome than all who stand around him?

You rule the swelling of the sea;
when its waves rise, you calm them.

You broke Rahab{d} in pieces like a corpse;
by your mighty arm your foes were scattered.

The heavens are yours; the earth too is yours;
the world and everything in it, you founded them.

North and south—you made them;
Tabor and Hermon ring out with joy in your name.

Yours is an arm with might;
your hand is strong; your right hand is lifted high.

Righteousness and justice are the base of your throne;
covenant love and faithfulness go ahead of your face.

Blessed is the people that knows the shout of celebration;
Yahweh, they will walk in the light of your face.

In your name they rejoice all the day,
and in your righteousness they are lifted up.

For you are the splendor of their might,
and through your goodwill our horn{e} is exalted.

For our shield belongs to Yahweh,
our king to the Holy One of Israel.

I have found David my servant;
with my holy oil I have anointed him.

My hand will stay with him;
my arm also will make him strong.

No enemy will get the better of him;
no son of wickedness will humble him.

I will beat down his foes in front of him
and strike those who hate him.

My faithfulness and my covenant love will be with him,
and in my name his horn will be lifted high.

I will set his hand on the sea
and his right hand on the rivers.

He will cry to me, ‘You are my Father,
my God, and the Rock of my salvation.’

And I will make him the firstborn,
highest of the kings of the earth.

I will keep my covenant love for him forever,
and my covenant with him will stand firm.

I will establish his offspring for all time,
and his throne like the days of the heavens.

If his children forsake my instruction
and do not live by my rulings,

if they profane my decrees
and fail to observe my commands,

then I will punish their transgression with the rod
and their iniquity with blows,

but I will not take away my covenant love from him{g}
or prove false to my faithfulness.

I will not violate my covenant
or change what has gone out from my lips.

Once for all I have sworn by my holiness;
I will not lie to David.

His offspring will endure forever,
and his throne like the sun before me.

Like the moon it will be established forever,
a faithful witness in the sky.”
Selah

But now you have cast off and spurned;
you are full of wrath against your anointed.

You have renounced the covenant with your servant;
you have dragged his crown in the dust.

You have breached every one of his walls;
you have left his fortresses in ruins.

Everyone passing by on the road robs him;
to his neighbors he has become an object of scorn.

You have lifted high the right hand of his adversaries;
you have given all his enemies cause to rejoice.

You have even turned back the edge of his sword
and have not held him up in battle.

You have ended his splendor
and hurled his throne to the ground.

How long, Yahweh? Will you hide yourself forever?
Will your wrath keep burning like fire?

Remember how fleeting my life is!
For what emptiness you have created all the children of man!

What man can live and not see death?
Who can rescue his soul from the power of Sheol?
Selah

Lord, where are your covenant loves of old,
which you swore to David in your faithfulness?

Remember, Lord, how your servants are taunted,
how I carry in my bosom the insults of all the many peoples,

with which your enemies taunt, Yahweh,
with which they taunt the footsteps of your anointed.

Blessed be Yahweh forever!
Amen and Amen.{h}

notes.text: Compare 1 Kings 4:31. The psalm celebrates God’s covenant with David (2 Samuel 7:8–16) and then laments its apparent collapse.
Or “the heavenly beings”; Hebrew bene ʾelim.
Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh.
A name for the sea monster of chaos, also used of Egypt; compare 87:4; Job 26:12.
So the qere; the ketiv has “you raise our horn.” The horn is a picture of strength.
Many Hebrew manuscripts have “your faithful one.”
So the Hebrew; some manuscripts and versions read “I will not remove.”
This doxology closes Book Three of the Psalms; compare 41:13; 72:18–19; 106:48.

chapters.heading: Book Four (Psalms 90–106)
chapters.title: A prayer of Moses, the man of God.{a}

verses.text:
Lord, you have been our home{b}
in generation after generation.

Before the mountains were born,
before you brought forth the earth and the world,
from everlasting to everlasting you are God.

You return mortals to dust{c}
and say, “Go back, children of Adam!”

You sweep them away; they are like a sleep,
like grass that springs up in the morning:

in the morning it blooms and springs up;
by evening it fades and dries out.

For we are spent by your anger;
by your fury we are terrified.

You have placed our iniquities in front of you,
our hidden sins in the light of your face.

For all our days slip away under your wrath;
we finish our years like a sigh.

Who knows the power of your anger,
and your wrath, as the fear of you deserves?

Teach us, then, to count our days,
that we may bring home a heart of wisdom.

Return, Yahweh! How long?
Have pity on your servants!

Fill us in the morning with your covenant love,
so that we may sing for joy and be glad through all our days.

Give us gladness for as many days as you have afflicted us,
for as many years as we have seen evil.

Let your servants see what you do,
and their sons your majesty.

Let the kindness{g} of the Lord our God be on us,
and make the work of our hands secure for us—
yes, make the work of our hands secure!

notes.text: Book Four of the Psalms begins here and closes with the doxology at 106:48. This is the only psalm attributed to Moses; compare Deuteronomy 33:1. From Book Four onward the Septuagint and Vulgate number most psalms one lower than the Hebrew (see the note on Psalm 9).
Or “refuge.”
Hebrew “to crushed matter”; compare Genesis 3:19.
Compare 2 Peter 3:8. A night watch was about four hours.
Hebrew “threescore years and ten, … fourscore.”
Or “their pride.”
Or “beauty.”

verses.text:
The one who lives in the hiding place of the Most High
will rest under the shade of the Almighty.{a}

I will say to Yahweh, “My refuge and my fortress,
my God, in whom I trust.”

For he will rescue you from the trap of the bird catcher
and from the deadly plague.

You need not dread the horror that comes by night,
or the arrow flying by day,

nor the plague that stalks in the dark,
nor the destruction that ravages at noon.

A thousand may fall at your side,
ten thousand at your right hand,
but it will not come near you.

You will only look on with your eyes
and see the payment of the wicked.

Because you have made Yahweh your refuge,{b}
the Most High your dwelling,

no evil will be allowed to meet you,
no plague will approach your tent.

For he will give his angels orders about you,
to guard you in all your ways.

They will lift you up in their hands,
lest you bruise your foot on a stone.{c}

You will tread on lion and cobra;
you will trample the young lion and the serpent.

“Because he clings to me in love, I will rescue him;
I will set him on high, because he knows my name.

With length of days I will satisfy him
and let him see my salvation.”

notes.text: Hebrew Shaddai. This psalm has no title; the Septuagint attributes it to David.
Hebrew “You, Yahweh, are my refuge”; the second line says that the Most High has been made the dwelling place.
Verses 11–12 are quoted in Matthew 4:6 and Luke 4:10–11.

chapters.title: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.

verses.text:
It is good to give thanks to Yahweh,
to sing praise to your name, O Most High,

to declare your covenant love in the morning,
and your faithfulness through the nights,

on the ten-stringed instrument and the harp,
to the murmuring music of the lyre.

For you, Yahweh, have gladdened me by what you have done;
at the works of your hands I sing for joy.

How great are your works, Yahweh!
How very deep are your thoughts!

The senseless man does not know it,
and the fool cannot grasp this:

that though the wicked spring up like grass
and all evildoers blossom,
it is for their destruction forever.
But you, Yahweh, are on high forever.

But you have raised my horn like that of the wild ox;
I am anointed with fresh oil.{a}

My eyes have looked on my foes;
my ears have heard the doom of the evildoers who rise against me.

The righteous will flourish like the palm tree
and grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.

Those planted in Yahweh’s house
will thrive in the courtyards of our God.

They still bear fruit in old age;
they stay full of sap and green,

to proclaim that Yahweh is upright;
he is my rock, and there is no wrong in him.{b}

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv has a variant spelling.

verses.text:
Your throne has been firm from of old;
you are from everlasting.

Mightier than the thunder of many waters,
mightier than the breakers of the sea,
is Yahweh on high!

notes.text: Or “Yahweh has become king.” Psalms 93 and 95–99 celebrate Yahweh’s kingship.

verses.text:
God of vengeance, Yahweh,
God of vengeance, shine out!

Lift yourself up, you judge of the earth;
pay back the arrogant as they have earned!

How long shall the wicked, Yahweh,
how long shall the wicked exult?

They pour out arrogant words;
all the evildoers boast.

They crush your people, Yahweh,
and oppress your inheritance.

They kill the widow and the foreigner,
and they murder the fatherless;

and they say, “Yah is not looking;
Jacob’s God pays no attention.”

Pay attention, you senseless among the people!
You fools, when will you become wise?

The one who set the ear in place—can he not hear?
The one who fashioned the eye—can he not see?

The one who corrects the nations—will he not punish?
The one who instructs mankind in knowledge—

Yahweh knows the thoughts of man,
that they are a mere breath.{a}

Happy is the man whom you discipline, Yah,
and whom you teach from your law,

granting him quiet in evil days,
while a pit is being dug for the wicked.

For Yahweh will not cast off his people;
he will not abandon his inheritance;

for justice will turn back to what is right,
and everyone honest in heart will follow it.

Who will stand up on my side against those who do evil?
Who will take my part against the workers of wrong?

Had Yahweh not come to help me,
my soul would quickly have settled in the silent land.

When I said, “My foot is slipping,”
your covenant love, Yahweh, held me up.

When my anxious thoughts are many within me,
your comforts delight my soul.

Can a seat of ruin be your partner,
which frames mischief by decree?

They gang up on the soul of the righteous
and declare innocent blood guilty.

But Yahweh has become my high fortress,
and my God the rock where I take refuge.

notes.text: Quoted in 1 Corinthians 3:20.

verses.text:
Come, let us sing for joy to Yahweh;
let us shout aloud to the Rock of our salvation!

Let us come before his face with thanksgiving;
let us shout to him with songs of praise!

For Yahweh is a great God,
and a great King above all gods.

The deep places of the earth lie in his hand;
the heights of the hills belong to him too.

The sea is his, for he made it,
and his hands formed the dry land.

Come, let us worship and bow low;
let us bend the knee before Yahweh, our Maker!

For he is our God,
and we are the people of his pasture,
the flock under his hand.
Today, if you would listen to his voice,

do not make your hearts stubborn as at Meribah,{a}
as that day at Massah{b} in the desert,

where your ancestors tested me
and put me on trial, though they had seen what I did.

For forty years I loathed that generation
and said, “They are a people whose hearts go astray,
and they have not known my ways.”

So I swore in my anger,
“They shall not enter my rest.”

notes.text: “Quarreling.”
“Testing.” Compare Exodus 17:1–7; Numbers 20:1–13. Verses 7–11 are quoted in Hebrews 3:7–11 and 4:3–7.

verses.text:
Sing to Yahweh a new song;{a}
sing to Yahweh, all the earth!

Sing to Yahweh; bless his name;
announce his salvation from day to day.

Tell of his glory among the nations,
his wonders among all the peoples.

For great is Yahweh, and highly to be praised;
he is to be feared above all gods.

For all the gods of the peoples are worthless idols,{b}
but Yahweh made the heavens.

Splendor and majesty are in front of him;
strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

Give to Yahweh, families of the peoples,
give to Yahweh glory and strength!

Give to Yahweh the glory his name deserves;
bring an offering and come into his courts!

Bow down to Yahweh in the splendor of holiness;{c}
tremble before him, all the earth!

Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice;
let the sea thunder, and all that fills it;

let the fields exult, and everything in them!
Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy

before Yahweh, for he comes,
for he comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness,
and the peoples in his faithfulness.

notes.text: Compare 1 Chronicles 16:23–33, which contains most of this psalm.
Hebrew ʾelilim, “nothings,” a wordplay on ʾelohim, “gods.”
Or “in holy attire.”

verses.text:
Yahweh reigns! Let the earth rejoice;
let the many coastlands be glad!

Clouds and thick darkness are around him;
righteousness and justice are the base of his throne.

Fire goes before him
and burns up his foes on every side.

His lightnings light up the world;
the earth sees and trembles.

The mountains melt like wax before Yahweh,
before the Lord of all the earth.

The heavens declare his righteousness,
and all the peoples see his glory.

For you, Yahweh, are Most High over all the earth;
you are exalted far above all gods.

Light has been sown{b} for the righteous one,
and gladness for those whose hearts are upright.

Rejoice in Yahweh, you righteous,
and give thanks to his holy name!{c}

notes.text: The Septuagint has “all his angels”; compare Hebrews 1:6.
So the Hebrew; one Hebrew manuscript and the ancient versions have “Light dawns.”
Hebrew “to the remembrance of his holiness.”

chapters.title: A psalm.

verses.text:
Sing to Yahweh a new song,
for he has done wonders!
His right hand and his holy arm
have won the victory for him.

Yahweh has made his salvation known;
before the eyes of the nations he has unveiled his righteousness.

He has remembered his covenant love and his faithfulness
toward the house of Israel.
All the ends of the earth have witnessed
the saving work of our God.

Raise a shout to Yahweh, all the earth!
Burst out in joyful song and make music!

Play to Yahweh on the lyre,
on the lyre, with the voice of melody!

With trumpets and the sound of the shofar,
raise a shout before the King, Yahweh!

Let the sea thunder, and everything in it,
the world, and those who live there!

Let the rivers clap their hands;
let the mountains sing out together for joy

before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness
and the peoples with equity.

Yahweh is king; let the nations shake!
He is seated between the cherubim; let the earth tremble!

Great is Yahweh in Zion;
high is he above all the peoples.

Let them praise your name, great and awesome.
Holy is he!{a}

Exalt Yahweh our God
and bow down at his footstool!
Holy is he!

Moses and Aaron were among his priests,
and Samuel among those who called on his name.
They called to Yahweh, and he answered them.

He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud;
they obeyed his laws and the rule he gave them.

Exalt Yahweh our God,
and bow down at his holy mountain,
for Yahweh our God is holy!

notes.text: The refrain “Holy is he” recurs in verses 5 and 9.
The Hebrew of this line is difficult.

chapters.title: A psalm for giving thanks.{a}

verses.text: Shout to Yahweh, all the earth!

Serve Yahweh with gladness!
Come into his presence with joyful singing!

Enter his gates with thanksgiving,
and his courts with praise!
Thank him; bless his name!

notes.text: Or “for the thank offering.”
So the qere (lo, “his”); the ketiv (loʾ, “not”) reads “and not we ourselves.”

chapters.title: Of David. A psalm.

verses.text:
I will sing of covenant love and justice;
to you, Yahweh, I will make music.

I will consider carefully the path that is blameless—
when will you visit me?
In my own house I will live
with a heart of integrity.

I will not set before my eyes
anything worthless.
I hate the deeds of those who turn aside;
they will not cling to me.

A crooked heart will be far from me;
I will have nothing to do with evil.

Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret,
I will silence him.{a}
Whoever has haughty eyes and a swollen heart,
I will not put up with him.

My eyes will rest on the faithful in the land,
that they may dwell beside me;
the one whose path is blameless
will minister to me.

No one who practices deceit
will live inside my house;
no one who tells lies
will stand firm before my eyes.

Each morning I will silence
the wicked of this land,
uprooting all evildoers
from the city of Yahweh.

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has a variant spelling of the same verb.

chapters.title: A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before Yahweh.

verses.text:
Yahweh, hear my prayer;
let my cry for help reach you!

Do not turn your face away from me
in my day of trouble!
Bend your ear to me;
when I call, be quick to answer!

For my days vanish like smoke,
and my bones glow like a furnace.

My heart is struck down and dried up like grass;
I even forget to eat my bread.

Because of my loud groaning
my bones stick to my flesh.

I am like a desert owl,{a}
like a little owl among the ruins.

I stay awake;
I am like a solitary bird on a rooftop.

My enemies insult me the whole day;
those who rage at me swear oaths by my name.

For I eat ashes as my bread
and mix tears into my drink,

because of your fury and your anger;
for you have lifted me up and thrown me away.

My days are like an evening shadow stretching out;
like grass I dry up.

But you, Yahweh, are enthroned forever;
your renown lasts through all generations.

For your servants hold her stones dear
