and pity her dust.

Nations will fear the name of Yahweh,
and all the kings of the earth your glory.

For Yahweh has built up Zion;
he has been seen in his glory.

He will turn to the prayer of the destitute
and will not despise their plea.

Let this be written down for a later generation,
so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah:

that he gazed down from his sanctuary on high;
Yahweh looked from heaven to the earth,

to hear the groans of prisoners,
to set free those condemned to die,

so that the name of Yahweh may be declared in Zion,
and his praise in Jerusalem,

when peoples gather together,
and kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.

He has humbled my strength on the road;{b}
he has shortened my days.

I say, “My God, do not take me away
in the middle of my days—
you whose years go on through all generations!

Long ago you founded the earth,
and the heavens are the work of your hands.{c}

but you are he who is,
and your years have no end.

The children of your servants will dwell secure,
and their offspring will be established before you.”

notes.text: The identification of these birds is uncertain.
So the qere; the ketiv reads “his strength.”

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul,
and all that is within me, bless his holy name!

Bless Yahweh, my soul,
and forget none of his kindnesses—

who pardons every one of your iniquities,
who cures every one of your sicknesses,

who buys back your life from the pit,
who sets a crown on you of covenant love and compassion,

who satisfies your years{a} with good,
so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.

Yahweh does righteous deeds
and justice for all the oppressed.

He made his ways known to Moses,
his deeds to the people of Israel.

Yahweh is compassionate and gracious,
slow to anger and rich in covenant love.{b}

He will not always accuse,
nor will he hold on to his anger forever.

He has not treated us as our sins deserve,
nor repaid us according to our iniquities.

For as high as the heavens are above the earth,
so mighty is his covenant love toward those who fear him;

as far as the sunrise is from the sunset,
so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

As a father has compassion on his children,
so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.

For he knows what we are made of;
he keeps in mind that we are dust.

Man—his days are like the grass;
like a wildflower, so he blossoms;

when the wind passes over it, it is gone,
and its place no longer recognizes it.

But the covenant love of Yahweh is from everlasting to everlasting
on those who fear him,
and his righteousness to children’s children,

for those who hold to his covenant
and keep his precepts in mind to do them.

Yahweh has set up his throne in the heavens,
and his kingdom rules over all.

Bless Yahweh, you his angels,
mighty in strength, who carry out his word,
obeying the voice of his word!

Bless Yahweh, all his hosts,
his ministers who carry out his desire!

Bless Yahweh, all his works,
in every place of his dominion!
Bless Yahweh, my soul!

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; traditionally “your mouth.”
Compare Exodus 34:6.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
Yahweh my God, you are very great!
You are clothed with splendor and majesty,

wrapping yourself in light as in a robe,
stretching out the heavens like a tent curtain.

he makes the winds his messengers,
flames of fire his servants.{a}

He fixed the earth on its bases,
so that it will not totter, forever and ever.

You covered it with the deep as with a garment;
the waters stood above the mountains.

They fled from your rebuke;
they ran in haste at your thunder’s voice.

The mountains rose, the valleys sank{b}
to the place you had appointed for them.

You set a boundary they may not cross,
so that they never again cover the earth.

You make springs gush out in the valleys;
they flow between the hills;

they give drink to every animal of the field;
the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

Beside them the birds of the heavens nest;
they sing among the branches.

From your upper rooms you water the mountains;
the earth is satisfied with the fruit of your work.

You cause grass to sprout for the livestock
and plants for the labor of mankind,
so that bread comes out of the earth,

and wine that gladdens the heart of man,
oil to make his face shine,
and bread that strengthens the heart of man.

The trees of Yahweh drink their fill,
the cedars of Lebanon that he planted,

There the birds make their nests;
the stork lives in the junipers.

The high mountains are for the wild goats;
the rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers.{c}

He made the moon for the set times;{d}
the sun knows its hour for going down.

You bring darkness, and it is night,
when all the beasts of the forest prowl.

Young lions roar after prey
and ask God for their food.

The sun comes up, and they slip away
to lie down in their lairs.

Man goes out to his work
and to his labor until evening.

There is the sea, great and wide,
teeming with creatures beyond number,
living things both small and great.

There ships go back and forth,
and Leviathan, whom you shaped to frolic there.{e}

All of them look to you
to give them their food in its season.

You give to them, and they gather;
you open your hand, and they are filled with good.

When you send out your Spirit,{f} they are created,
and you renew the face of the ground.

May the glory of Yahweh last forever;
may Yahweh rejoice in his works,

He looks on the earth, and it quakes;
he touches the mountains, and smoke rises!

All my life I will sing to Yahweh;
I will sing praise to my God while I live.

May my meditation be pleasing to him;
as for me, I rejoice in Yahweh.

Let sinners vanish from the earth,
and let the wicked be no more!
Bless Yahweh, my soul!
Hallelujah!{g}

notes.text: Or “he makes his angels winds.” Quoted in Hebrews 1:7.
Or “They went up the mountains and went down into the valleys.”
Hebrew shephanim, the rock hyrax.
Or “the appointed festivals.”
Or “to play with.” Compare Job 41:5.
Or “your breath.”

Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh. This is the first occurrence of the word in the Bible; it recurs in Psalms 105–106, 111–113, 115–117, 135, and 146–150, and in Revelation 19:1–6. CJT keeps the familiar transliteration “Hallelujah.”

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name;{a}
make his deeds known among the peoples!

Sing to him, make music to him;
ponder all his wonders!

Take pride in his holy name;
may the hearts that seek Yahweh rejoice!

Search for Yahweh and his strength;
seek his face always!

Remember the wonders he has worked,
his signs, and the judgments he has spoken,

you offspring of Abraham, his servant,
you children of Jacob, his chosen ones!

He is Yahweh our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.

He remembers his covenant forever,
the word he decreed for a thousand generations,

the covenant he made with Abraham,
his sworn promise to Isaac,

He made it firm for Jacob as an ordinance,
an everlasting covenant for Israel,

declaring, “The land of Canaan I give to you,
your allotted inheritance.”

When they were few in number,
a mere handful, and foreigners in it,

wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,

he let no one oppress them;
he rebuked kings on their account:

“Do not touch my anointed ones,
and do my prophets no harm!”

He called down a famine over the country
and snapped every supply of bread.{b}

Ahead of them he had sent a man:
Joseph, sold into slavery.

They hurt his feet with shackles;
his neck{c} was put in iron,

until the time that his word came true;
the word of Yahweh tested him.

The king gave the order to loose him;
the one who ruled the peoples released him.

He made him lord over his household
and ruler over all his possessions,

to bind his princes at his will
and to teach his elders wisdom.

Israel then entered Egypt;
Jacob stayed as an alien in Ham’s land.{d}

And God made his people very fruitful
and made them stronger than their foes.

He turned their hearts to hate his people,
to deal craftily with his servants.

He sent Moses, his servant,
and Aaron, whom he had chosen.

They performed his signs among them,{e}
and wonders in the land of Ham.

He sent darkness and made it dark;
did they not rebel against his words?{f}

He turned their waters into blood
and made their fish die.

Their land swarmed with frogs,
even in the rooms of their kings.

He spoke, and swarms of flies came,
and gnats throughout their territory.

He gave them hail in place of rain,
and flashes of fire throughout their land.

He battered their vines and their fig trees
and splintered the trees throughout their borders.

He spoke, and the locusts came,
young locusts without number,

which devoured all the vegetation in their land
and ate up the fruit of their ground.

He struck down every firstborn in their land,
the first fruits of all their vigor.

Then he brought Israel out with silver and gold,
and among his tribes no one stumbled.

Egypt was glad when they left,
for dread of Israel had fallen on them.

He stretched a cloud over them for a screen
and fire to give light by night.

They made a request, and he sent quail,
and filled them with heaven’s bread.

He opened the rock, and water gushed out;
it ran through the dry land like a river.

For he remembered his holy word
to Abraham, his servant.

He led his people out rejoicing,
his chosen with songs of joy.

He gave them the lands of the nations,
and they took possession of what the peoples had toiled for,

notes.text: Verses 1–15 appear also in 1 Chronicles 16:8–22.
That is, the food supply.
Hebrew nephesh, “his soul” or “his throat.” So the qere; the ketiv has “his foot” in the previous line.
A poetic name for Egypt; compare Genesis 10:6.
Hebrew “They set among them the words of his signs.”
So the qere (and the Septuagint and Syriac omit “not”: “they rebelled against his words”). The ketiv reads “his word.” The sense of the line is debated.

verses.text:
Who can tell of the mighty deeds of Yahweh
or make all his praise heard?

Happy are those who keep justice,
who do righteousness at all times!

Remember me, Yahweh, when you show favor to your people;
visit me with your salvation,

that I may see the prosperity of your chosen ones,
that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation,
that I may boast along with your inheritance.

We have sinned, as our fathers did;
we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.

Yet he saved them for the sake of his name,
to make his might known.

He rebuked the Red Sea, and it became dry;
he guided them through the depths as if through open country.

He rescued them from those who hated them
and redeemed them from their enemy’s grip.

The waters closed over their foes;
not a single one survived.

Then they believed his words;
they sang his praise.

How soon they forgot what he had done!
They would not wait for his plan.

In the wilderness they were seized with greed
and tested God in the barren land.

So he granted their request,
yet he sent a wasting into their souls.

In the camp they grew jealous of Moses
and of Aaron, the holy one of Yahweh.

The earth opened and swallowed Dathan
and covered the company of Abiram.

Fire blazed out among their company;
flame burned up the wicked.

They made a calf at Horeb
and bowed down to a cast image.

They traded away their Glory{c}
for the likeness of a grass-eating bull.

They forgot God, their Savior,
who had done great things in Egypt,

wondrous works in the land of Ham,
awesome deeds at the Red Sea.

So he said he would destroy them—
had not Moses, his chosen one,
stood in the breach before him,
to turn his wrath away from destroying them.

Then they scorned the desirable land;
they put no faith in his promise.

They muttered in their tents
and would not heed Yahweh’s voice.

So he lifted his hand to them in an oath
to bring them down in the wilderness,

and make their offspring fall among the nations,
and scatter them throughout the lands.

They attached themselves to Baal of Peor
and ate offerings made to the dead.{d}

Their deeds provoked him to anger,
and plague burst out on them.

But Phinehas rose and stepped in to judge,
and the plague was held back.

It was credited to him as righteousness
for all generations, forever.

They angered him at the waters of Meribah,
and it went badly for Moses because of them,

because they made his spirit bitter,
and rash words came from his lips.

They did not destroy the peoples,
as Yahweh had commanded them,

but they intermingled with the nations
and adopted their ways.

They served their idols,
which became a snare to them.

They sacrificed their sons
and their daughters to demons.

They poured out innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters,
whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan,
and the land was defiled with bloodshed.

So they became unclean by their deeds
and prostituted themselves in their practices.

Then the anger of Yahweh burned against his people,
and he loathed his own inheritance.

He gave them into the hand of the nations,
and those who hated them ruled over them.

Their enemies oppressed them,
and they were humbled under their power.

Many times he rescued them,
but they were rebellious in their plans
and sank low through their iniquity.

Yet he looked on their distress
when he heard their cry.

He called to mind his covenant for their sake
and had a change of heart in his abundant covenant love.{e}

He made all their captors
feel pity for them.

Save us, Yahweh our God!
Gather us out of the nations
to thank your holy name
and to take pride in praising you.

Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
And let all the people say, “Amen!”
Hallelujah!{f}

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35. Verses 1 and 47–48 appear also in 1 Chronicles 16:34–36.
Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds,” here and in verses 9 and 22.
That is, God. An ancient scribal tradition records that the original reading was “my glory.”
Or “to lifeless gods.” Compare Numbers 25:1–9.
So the qere (plural, “his many acts of covenant love”); the ketiv is singular.
This doxology closes Book Four of the Psalms; compare 41:13, 72:18–19, and 89:52. Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!”

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good,
for his covenant love lasts forever!{a}

Let the redeemed of Yahweh say so,
those he redeemed from the grip of the foe

Some wandered in the wilderness, in the desert wastes;
they found no road to a city where they could settle.

Hungry and thirsty,
their souls grew faint within them.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he rescued them from their distress.

He led them by a straight path
until they reached a city to live in.

Let them thank Yahweh for his covenant love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!{c}

For he satisfies the thirsty soul,
and the hungry soul he fills with good things.

Some sat in darkness and deep gloom,{d}
prisoners in misery and chains,

because they had rebelled against God’s words
and scorned the plan of the Most High.

So he humbled their hearts with hard labor;
they stumbled, and no one helped.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he saved them from their distress.

He brought them out of darkness and deep gloom
and tore their chains apart.

Let them thank Yahweh for his covenant love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!

For he has broken down gates of bronze
and hacked through iron bars.

Some were fools in their rebellious ways
and suffered for their iniquities;

their appetite turned against all food,
and they drew near to death’s gates.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he saved them from their distress.

He sent out his word and healed them
and rescued them from their pits.

Let them thank Yahweh for his covenant love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!

Let them bring thank offerings in sacrifice
and recount his works with shouts of joy!

Some went down to the sea in ships,
doing their trade on the mighty waters;

they saw the works of Yahweh,
his wonders in the deep.

For he spoke and raised up a stormy wind,
which lifted high the waves.

They rose to the sky; they plunged to the depths;
their courage melted in their peril.

They reeled and lurched like drunkards,
and all their skill was swallowed up.

Then they cried out to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he brought them out of their distress.

He made the gale grow calm,
and the sea’s waves{e} fell silent.

They were glad when it grew quiet,
and he guided them to the harbor they longed for.

Let them thank Yahweh for his covenant love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!

Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people
and praise him in the council of the elders!

He turns rivers into desert,
springs of water into thirsty ground,

a fruitful land into a salt flat,
because of the evil of those who live there.

He turns desert into pools of water,
parched land into springs.

There he settles the hungry,
and they build a city to live in;

they sow fields and plant vineyards
and gather a fruitful harvest.

He blesses them so that they increase greatly,
and he keeps their livestock from growing few.

When they are diminished and brought low
through oppression, trouble, and sorrow,

he heaps scorn on princes
and sends them wandering in pathless wastes;{f}

but he raises the poor up from misery
and multiplies their clans like sheep.

The upright look on and rejoice,
and every wrongdoer’s mouth is stopped.

Whoever is wise, let him heed these things,
and let them consider the covenant love of Yahweh.

notes.text: Book Five of the Psalms begins here and runs to the closing doxology of Psalm 150. It contains the Songs of Ascents (120–134), the Hallel psalms (113–118), the acrostic Psalm 119, and the closing Hallelujah psalms (146–150).
That is, from the south; the Hebrew has “from the sea.”
This refrain recurs in verses 15, 21, and 31.

chapters.title: A song. A psalm of David.{a}

verses.text:
My heart is steadfast, God;
I will sing and make music with all my being.{b}

Awake, harp and lyre!
I will awaken the dawn.

I will thank you among the peoples, Yahweh;
I will make music to you among the nations.

For your covenant love is great above the heavens,
and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

Be exalted above the heavens, God,
and let your glory be over all the earth!

That those you love may be rescued,
save with your right hand and answer me!

Who will lead me into the walled city?
Who will guide me as far as Edom?

Have you not rejected us, God?
You do not go out, God, with our armies.

Help us against the enemy,
for human help is useless.

With God we will act with valor,
and he will tread our enemies underfoot.

notes.text: This psalm combines 57:7–11 (verses 1–5) and 60:5–12 (verses 6–13), with small differences.
Hebrew “even my glory.”
Or “in his sanctuary.”

chapters.title: To the director. Of David. A psalm.

verses.text: God whom I praise, do not keep silent!

With words of hate they hem me in
and fight me for no reason.

My love they answer with accusation,
while I keep praying.{a}

They repay me evil for good,
and hatred for my love.

“Set a wicked man in authority over him;
let an accuser{b} take his place at his right side.

When he is tried, let him come out guilty;
let his prayer be counted as sin.

Let his days be few;
let another take his position.{c}

Let his children be fatherless
and his wife a widow.

Let his children wander and beg,
searching for food far from their ruined homes.{d}

Let the creditor seize all he has;
let strangers plunder the fruit of his toil.

Let no one extend covenant love to him,
nor anyone pity his fatherless children.

Let his descendants be cut off;
in the next generation let their name be wiped out.

Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before Yahweh,
and let the sin of his mother not be wiped out.

Let them be before Yahweh continually,
that he may cut off their memory from the earth,

since he never thought to show covenant love,
but chased down the poor and the needy
and the crushed in heart, to kill them.

He loved cursing—let it fall on him!
Blessing gave him no pleasure—let it stay far from him!

Let it wrap him like his cloak,
like the sash he ties on day after day!”

May this be the reward of my accusers from Yahweh,
of those who speak evil against my life!

For I am poor and needy,
and my heart is pierced within me.

Like an evening shadow I am slipping away;
I am brushed off like a locust.

Fasting has made my knees weak;
my flesh has wasted away, lean and bare.

I have become an object of scorn to them;
when they see me, they shake their heads.

Help me, Yahweh my God!
Save me according to your covenant love!

Let them know that your hand is in this;
you, Yahweh, have done it!

Let them curse, but you will bless!
They rose up, but they will be put to shame,
and your servant will be glad.

Let my accusers be clothed with disgrace;
let them wear their shame like a cloak!

With my mouth I will give great thanks to Yahweh;
in the midst of the crowd I will praise him.

For he stands at the right hand of the needy,
to save him from those who would condemn his soul.

notes.text: Hebrew “but I—prayer.”

Hebrew satan. Many interpreters take verses 6–19 as the curses spoken by the psalmist’s enemies against him (note “they say” implied in verse 6 and “my accusers” in verse 20); others take them as the psalmist’s own words.
Quoted in Acts 1:20.
So the Hebrew; the Septuagint reads “let them be driven out of their ruins.”

chapters.title: Of David. A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh will send out your mighty scepter from Zion:
“Rule in the midst of your enemies!”

Your people will volunteer
on the day you muster your forces,
in holy splendor;{b}
out of the womb of the dawn
you will have the dew of your youth.

The Lord is at your right side;
he will crush kings on the day he is angry.

From the stream beside the road he will drink,
and so he will raise his head high.

notes.text: Hebrew neʾum YHWH laʾdoni. The first is the divine name Yahweh; the second is ʾadoni, “my lord, my master,” a title of honor used of kings and superiors (not the divine title ʾAdonai). Traditional English Bibles print “The LORD said unto my Lord,” hiding the difference. Jesus cites this verse to show that the Messiah is more than David’s son (Matthew 22:41–45; Mark 12:35–37; Luke 20:41–44); see also Acts 2:34–35, 1 Corinthians 15:25, and Hebrews 1:13. Psalm 110 is the Old Testament passage most often quoted or alluded to in the New Testament.
So many Hebrew manuscripts; others read “on the holy mountains.” The Hebrew of this verse is difficult.
Or “on account of Melchizedek.” Compare Genesis 14:18–20; quoted in Hebrews 5:6, 6:20, and 7:17, 21.

verses.text:
Great are the works of Yahweh,
studied by all who delight in them.

Splendid and majestic is his work,
and his righteousness stands forever.

He has made his wonders to be remembered;
Yahweh is gracious and compassionate.

He gives food to those who fear him;
he remembers his covenant forever.

The might of his deeds he has made known to his people,
handing them the heritage of the nations.

The works of his hands are faithfulness and justice;
all his precepts are trustworthy.

They are upheld forever and ever,
carried out in faithfulness and uprightness.

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” (see 104:35). After the opening Hallelujah, Psalms 111 and 112 are matched acrostic poems: each of their twenty-two half-lines begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The other acrostics in the Psalter are 9–10, 25, 34, 37, 119, and 145.
Compare Proverbs 1:7; 9:10.

verses.text:
His offspring will be mighty in the land;
the generation of the upright will be blessed.

Wealth and riches are in his house,
and his righteousness stands forever.

For the upright a light rises in the dark—
gracious, merciful, and just.

It goes well with the man who is generous and lends,
who conducts his affairs with justice.

For he will never be shaken;
the righteous will be remembered forever.

Evil tidings hold no terror for him;
his heart stands steady, relying on Yahweh.

His heart is steady; he will not fear,
until he looks in triumph on his foes.

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” Like Psalm 111, this psalm is an acrostic; it describes the righteous person in terms Psalm 111 uses of God (compare 111:3, 4 with 112:3, 4).
Quoted in 2 Corinthians 9:9.

verses.text:
Blessed be the name of Yahweh
from now on and forevermore!

From where the sun rises to where it sets,
let the name of Yahweh be praised!

Yahweh is high above all nations,
his glory above the heavens.

Who is like Yahweh our God,
who is seated on high,

who stoops down to look
on the heavens and the earth?

He lifts the lowly up out of the dust
and raises the poor from the refuse pile,

to seat them with princes,
with the princes of his people.

He gives the childless woman a home,
a joyful mother of children.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” Psalms 113–118 form the “Egyptian Hallel,” sung at the great festivals and especially at Passover, when 113–114 were sung before the meal and 115–118 after it (compare Matthew 26:30; Mark 14:26).

verses.text:
When Israel came out of Egypt,
the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech,

Judah became his sanctuary,
Israel his dominion.

The sea saw and ran away;
the Jordan drew back.{a}

The mountains skipped like rams,
the hills like young sheep.

Sea, what made you run away?
Jordan, why did you draw back?

Mountains, that you skip like rams?
Hills, like young sheep?

Earth, writhe before the presence of the Lord,
before the presence of Jacob’s God,

who turns the rock into a pool of water,
the flint into a flowing spring.{b}

notes.text: Compare Exodus 14:21–22 and Joshua 3:14–17.
The Septuagint, Vulgate, and some Hebrew manuscripts join Psalms 114 and 115 as one psalm (see the note on Psalm 9).

verses.text:
Not to us, Yahweh, not to us,
but to your name give glory,
because of your covenant love and your faithfulness!

Why should the nations say,
“Where, now, is their God?”

Our God is in the heavens;
he does whatever he pleases.

Their idols are silver and gold,
made by human hands.

They have a mouth, yet no speech;
they have eyes, yet no sight.

They have ears, yet no hearing;
they have a nose, yet no sense of smell.

Their makers will be just like them,
as will everyone who relies on them.{a}

Israel, trust in Yahweh!
He is their help and their shield.

House of Aaron, trust in Yahweh!
He is their help and their shield.

You who fear Yahweh, trust in Yahweh!
He is their help and their shield.

He will bless those who fear Yahweh,
both small and great.

May Yahweh give you increase,
you and your children!

May you be blessed by Yahweh,
the Maker of heaven and earth!

The heavens are the heavens of Yahweh,
but the earth he has given to the children of Adam.

The dead do not praise Yah,
nor do any who go down into silence.

notes.text: Verses 4–8 are closely paralleled in 135:15–18.
Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” (see 104:35).

verses.text:
I love Yahweh, because he hears
my voice and my pleas for mercy.

Because he has turned his ear to me,
I will call on him as long as I live.

Then I called on the name of Yahweh:
“Please, Yahweh, rescue my soul!”

Gracious is Yahweh, and righteous;
our God is compassionate.

Yahweh keeps watch over the simple;
I was laid low, and he rescued me.

Return, my soul, to your rest,
for Yahweh has dealt generously with you.

For you have rescued my soul from death,
my eyes from tears,
my feet from stumbling.

I will walk before Yahweh
in the land of the living.

I believed, even when I said,{b}
“I am greatly afflicted”;

In my panic I said,
“Every human being is a liar.”

What shall I give back to Yahweh
for all his benefits to me?

I will lift up the cup of salvation
and call on the name of Yahweh.

I will fulfill my vows to Yahweh
in the presence of all his people.

Precious in the eyes of Yahweh
is the death of his faithful ones.

To you I will bring a thank offering in sacrifice
and invoke the name of Yahweh.

I will fulfill my vows to Yahweh
in the presence of all his people,

in the courts of the house of Yahweh,
in your midst, Jerusalem.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: The realm of the dead.
Or “I believed, therefore I spoke.” The Septuagint begins a new psalm here (its Psalm 115); quoted in 2 Corinthians 4:13.

verses.text:
Praise Yahweh, all you nations!
Extol him, all you peoples!{a}

For his covenant love toward us is mighty,
and the faithfulness of Yahweh endures forever.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: The shortest psalm and the shortest chapter in the Bible. Quoted in Romans 15:11.

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good;
his covenant love lasts forever!

Let Israel say,
“His covenant love lasts forever.”

Let the house of Aaron say,
“His covenant love lasts forever.”

Let those who fear Yahweh say,
“His covenant love lasts forever.”

Out of my distress I called on Yah;
Yah answered me and set me in a wide place.{a}

Yahweh is for me; I will not fear.
What can man do to me?{b}

Yahweh is for me as my helper;
I will look in triumph on those who hate me.

It is better to take refuge in Yahweh
than to trust in man.

It is better to take refuge in Yahweh
than to trust in princes.

All the nations surrounded me;
in Yahweh’s name I destroyed them!

They surrounded me, yes, surrounded me;
in the name of Yahweh I cut them off!

I was thrust at hard, to make me fall,{c}
but Yahweh came to my help.

Yah is my strength and my song,
and he has become my salvation.{d}

A sound of glad shouts and salvation
is in the tents of the righteous:
“The right hand of Yahweh does mighty things!

The right hand of Yahweh is lifted high;
the right hand of Yahweh does mighty things!”

I will not die, but I will live
and tell of the works of Yah.

Yah has disciplined me severely,
but he has not handed me over to death.

Open for me the gates of righteousness;
I will go in through them and thank Yah.

This is the gate of Yahweh;
the righteous will go in through it.

I thank you that you answered me
and have become my salvation.

The stone that the builders rejected
has become the cornerstone.{e}

This has come from Yahweh;
it is wonderful in our eyes.

This is the day that Yahweh has made;
let us rejoice and be glad in it.

Please, Yahweh, save us!{f}
Please, Yahweh, give us success!

Blessed is he who comes in the name of Yahweh!{g}
We bless you from the house of Yahweh.

Yahweh is God,
and he has given us light.
Bind the festal sacrifice with cords,
up to the horns of the altar!{h}

You are my God, and I will thank you;
my God, I will exalt you.

Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good;
his covenant love lasts forever!

notes.text: Hebrew merkhav-yah, “a broad place of Yah.”
Quoted in Hebrews 13:6.
Hebrew “You pushed me hard”; the Septuagint and Syriac read “I was pushed.”
Quoted from Exodus 15:2; compare Isaiah 12:2.
Hebrew “the head of the corner.” Verses 22–23 are quoted in the New Testament: in Matthew 21:42, in Mark 12:10–11, in Luke 20:17, in Acts 4:11 and in 1 Peter 2:7.
Hebrew hoshiʿah na, the source of the word “Hosanna” (Matthew 21:9; Mark 11:9–10; John 12:13).
Quoted in Matthew 21:9; 23:39; Mark 11:9; Luke 13:35; 19:38; John 12:13.
The meaning of this line is uncertain.

verses.text:
Happy are the people of blameless conduct,{a}
who live by the instruction of Yahweh!

Happy are they who guard his testimonies,
who search for him with a whole heart,

who never practice wrongdoing,
but keep walking in his ways!

You have laid down your precepts
to be kept with care.

Oh, that my ways were steady
in keeping your statutes!

Then I would not be put to shame,
when I fix my eyes on all your commandments.

With uprightness of heart I will praise you
while I learn the judgments of your righteousness.

Your statutes I will keep;
do not abandon me completely!

How can a young man keep his path pure?
By guarding it according to your word.

With all my heart I have sought you;
do not let me stray from your commandments!

Within my heart I have stored up your promise,
to keep me from sinning against you.

Blessed are you, Yahweh;
teach me your statutes!

With my lips I recount
all the judgments of your mouth.

In the way of your testimonies I rejoice
as much as in all riches.

On your precepts I will reflect
and keep your paths before my eyes.

I will delight in your statutes;
I will not forget your word.

Deal generously with your servant,
that I may live and keep your word.

Uncover my eyes, that I may see
wonders out of your law.

I am only a stranger in the land;
do not conceal your commandments from me!

My soul is crushed with longing
for your judgments at all times.

You rebuke the arrogant, the cursed,
who stray from your commandments.

Roll scorn and contempt off me,
for I have kept your testimonies.

Even if princes sit and talk against me,
your servant will meditate on your statutes.

Your testimonies are what I delight in;
they are the men of my counsel.

My soul lies stuck in the dust;
revive me as your word has said!

I told you my ways, and you answered me;
teach me your statutes!

Help me grasp the way of your precepts,
so that I may reflect on your wondrous works.

My soul weeps{b} from sorrow;
raise me up according to your word!

Keep the way of falsehood far from me,
and graciously give me your law!

I have chosen the way of faithfulness;
I have set your judgments before me.

I cling to your testimonies, Yahweh;
do not put me to shame!

I will run the way of your commandments,
for you enlarge my heart.

Yahweh, instruct me in the way your statutes go,
and I will guard it to the last.{c}

Give me understanding, and I will keep your law
and observe it with all my heart.

Lead me in the path of your commandments,
for I delight in it.

Bend my heart toward your testimonies
and away from greedy profit!

Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things;
give me life in your ways.{d}

Fulfill to your servant your promise,
which leads to the fear of you.

Turn away the disgrace that I dread,
for your judgments are good.

See how I yearn for your precepts!
Revive me by your righteousness!

Let your covenant love come to me, Yahweh,
your salvation according to your promise;

so that I can reply to those who mock me,
because I rely on your word.

Do not take the word of truth wholly out of my mouth,
for I hope in your judgments.

I will keep your law continually,
forever and ever.

I will go about at liberty,
because your precepts are what I seek.

I will speak of your testimonies before kings
and will not be put to shame.

I will delight in your commandments,
which I love.

I lift my hands toward your commandments, which I love,
and I reflect on your statutes.

Remember the promise to your servant,
the one that gave me hope.

This is my comfort in my affliction:
your promise gives me life.

The arrogant utterly mock me,
but I do not turn aside from your law.

I remember your judgments from of old, Yahweh,
and I take comfort.

Hot indignation seizes me because of the wicked,
who forsake your law.

Your statutes have been my songs
in the house of my sojourning.

I remember your name in the night, Yahweh,
and I keep your law.

This has been my lot,
that I have kept your precepts.

My share is Yahweh;
I have said that I will keep your words.

With all my heart I have entreated your face;
show me grace as you have promised.

I have thought about my ways
and turned my steps back to your statutes.

I make haste without lingering
to keep your commandments.

The cords of the wicked wrap around me,
but I do not forget your law.

At midnight I rise to thank you
for your righteous judgments.

I am a companion of all who fear you,
of those who keep your precepts.

The earth, Yahweh, is full of your covenant love;
teach me your statutes!

You have dealt well with your servant,
Yahweh, according to your word.

Teach me good discernment and knowledge,
for I believe in your commandments.

Before I was afflicted I went astray,
but now I keep your promise.

You are good and do good;
teach me your statutes!

The arrogant smear me with lies,
but with all my heart I keep your precepts.

Their heart is thick like fat,
but I delight in your law.

It was good for me that I was afflicted,
so that I might learn your statutes.

The law of your mouth is better to me
than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

Your hands have made and shaped me;
give me understanding, that I may learn your commandments.

Those who fear you will see me and rejoice,
because I hope in your word.

I know, Yahweh, that your judgments are righteous,
and that in faithfulness you have afflicted me.

May your covenant love be my consolation,
as you promised your servant.

Let your compassion come to me, that I may live,
for your law is my delight.

May the proud be ashamed for twisting things against me with lies;
I will reflect on your instructions.

May those who fear you come back to me,
even those who know{e} your testimonies.

May my heart be whole in your statutes,
so that shame never comes on me.

My soul faints for your salvation;
I hope in your word.

My eyes grow dim waiting for your promise;
“When will you console me?” I say.

Though I am like a wineskin shriveled by smoke,
your statutes have not slipped my mind.

How many are the days of your servant?
When will you bring judgment on those who persecute me?

The arrogant have dug pits for me,
people who do not live by your law.

All your commandments are faithful;
they persecute me with lies; help me!

They almost wiped me from the earth,
yet I have not let go of your precepts.

In your covenant love give me life,
and I will keep the testimony of your mouth.

Forever, Yahweh,
your word stands firm in the heavens.

Your faithfulness lasts through all generations;
you established the earth, and it stands.

By your judgments they stand to this day,
for all things are your servants.

If your law had not been my delight,
I would have perished in my affliction.

Never will I forget your precepts,
for through them you have revived me.

I am yours; save me,
for I have sought your precepts.

The wicked wait to destroy me,
but I give thought to your testimonies.

I have seen a limit to all perfection,
but your commandment is boundless.

Oh, how I love your law!
It is my meditation all day long.

Your commandment gives me more wisdom than my foes,
for it is mine forever.

I have more insight than all my teachers,
for your testimonies are my meditation.

I understand more than the elders,
for I keep your precepts.

I hold back my feet from every evil path,
so that I may keep your word.

From your judgments I have not swerved,
for it is you who have instructed me.

How sweet your promises are to my taste,
sweeter than honey to my mouth!

From your precepts I gain understanding;
therefore I hate every false path.

A lamp to my feet is your word,
a light along my path.

I have taken an oath and will carry it out:
to keep the judgments of your righteousness.

I am suffering terribly;
Yahweh, revive me as you promised!

Accept, Yahweh, the freewill offerings of my mouth,
and teach me your judgments.

I carry my life in my hands continually,{f}
but your law I do not forget.

The wicked have laid a snare for me,
but from your precepts I have not wandered.

Your testimonies are my inheritance forever,
for they are the joy of my heart.

I have bent my heart to do your statutes
forever, to the end.

Those with a divided heart I hate;
your law is what I love.

You are my hiding place and my shield;
I hope in your word.

Away from me, you evildoers,
so that I may keep the commandments of my God!

Uphold me as you promised, so that I live,
and do not let my hope end in shame!

Support me, and I will be rescued;
I will keep my gaze on your statutes always.

You reject all who stray from your statutes,
for their deceitfulness is futile.

You remove the wicked of the earth like slag;
that is why I love your testimonies.

My flesh shudders for dread of you,
and I am afraid of your judgments.

I have done what is just and right;
do not abandon me to my oppressors!

Guarantee your servant’s welfare;
do not let the arrogant oppress me!

My eyes fail with watching for your salvation
and for your righteous promise.

Deal with your servant according to your covenant love,
and teach me your statutes.

I am your servant; give me understanding,
that I may know your testimonies!

It is time for Yahweh to act,
for your law has been broken.

Therefore I love your commandments
more than gold, more than fine gold.

Therefore I count all your precepts right in everything;{g}
I hate every false path.

Your testimonies are wonderful;
therefore my soul keeps them.

The unfolding of your words gives light;
it gives understanding to the simple.

I open my mouth wide and pant,
for I long for your commandments.

Turn toward me and show me grace,
as is right for those who love your name.

Make my steps firm by your promise,
and let no iniquity rule over me.

Ransom me from the oppression of men,
and I will keep your precepts.

Let your face shine on your servant,
and instruct me in your statutes.

My eyes pour down rivers of water
because your law goes unkept.

Righteous are you, Yahweh,
and upright are your judgments.

In righteousness you have commanded your testimonies,
in utter faithfulness.

My zeal has worn me out,
for my adversaries have forgotten your words.

Your promise is well tested,
and your servant loves it.

Insignificant and scorned though I am,
I have not forgotten your precepts.

Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness,
and your instruction is truth.

Trouble and anguish have found me,
but your commandments are my delight.

Your testimonies are righteous forever;
give me understanding, that I may live.

I call with all my heart; answer me, Yahweh!
I will keep your statutes.

To you I call out—rescue me,
so that I may guard your testimonies.

I rise before dawn and cry for help;
I hope in your words.{h}

My eyes are awake before the night watches,
that I may meditate on your promise.

Hear my voice according to your covenant love;
Yahweh, give me life according to your justice.

Those who pursue evil schemes draw near;
they are far from your law.

You are near, Yahweh,
and all your commandments are truth.

Long ago I learned from your testimonies
that you founded them forever.

Look on my affliction and rescue me,
for I do not forget your law.

Take up my case and redeem me;
revive me as you have promised!

Far from the wicked is salvation,
because they do not search out your statutes.

Great is your compassion, Yahweh;
give me life according to your judgments.

Many are my persecutors and my foes,
but I do not swerve from your testimonies.

I look at the faithless and feel disgust,
because they do not keep your promise.

Look how I love your instructions!
Yahweh, revive me in keeping with your steadfast love.

The sum of your word is truth,
and every one of your righteous judgments lasts forever.

Princes persecute me without cause,
but my heart stands in awe of your words.{i}

I rejoice at your promise
like one who finds great plunder.

Falsehood I hate and detest;
your law I love.

Seven times a day I praise you
for your righteous judgments.

Great peace belongs to those who love your law;
nothing makes them stumble.

I hope for your salvation, Yahweh,
and I do your commandments.

My soul keeps your testimonies;
I love them greatly.

I have kept your precepts and your testimonies,
since all my ways lie open before you.

Let my cry come near before you, Yahweh;
give me understanding according to your word!

Let my plea come before you;
rescue me according to your promise!

My lips will pour out praise,
for you teach me your statutes.

Let my tongue sing out your promise,
since every commandment of yours is righteous.

Let your hand be ready to help me,
for I have chosen your precepts.

I long for your salvation, Yahweh,
and your law is my delight.

May my soul live to praise you,
and may your judgments come to my aid.

I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek your servant,
for I do not forget your commandments.

notes.text: Psalm 119 is the longest psalm and the longest chapter in the Bible. It is an acrostic in twenty-two stanzas, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet; each of the eight lines in a stanza begins with that stanza’s letter. Nearly every verse names God’s word with one of eight terms: law (torah), testimonies, precepts, statutes, commandments, judgments, word (dabar), and promise or saying (ʾimrah).
Or “drips away,” “melts.”
Or “as my reward.”
So many Hebrew manuscripts; the Masoretic Text reads “your way.”
So the qere; the ketiv reads “that they may know.”
That is, constantly in danger.
The Hebrew of this line is difficult.
So the qere; the ketiv reads “your word.”
So the qere; the ketiv reads “your word.”

chapters.title: A song of ascents.{a}

verses.text:
To Yahweh I called in my trouble,
and he answered me.

Yahweh, rescue my soul from lying lips,
from a tongue of deceit!

What shall he give you, what further shall he add to you,
O lying tongue?

A warrior’s sharpened arrows,
with glowing coals of the broom tree!

Woe to me, that I live as an alien in Meshech,
that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!{b}

Too long my soul has had its home
with those who hate peace.

I am for peace, but when I speak,
they are for war.

notes.text: Psalms 120–134 each carry the title “A song of ascents” (Hebrew shir hammaʿalot). They are widely understood as songs sung by pilgrims “going up” to Jerusalem for the festivals; Jewish tradition also linked them with the fifteen steps of the temple. Psalm 121’s title has a slightly different wording (“A song for the ascents”).
Meshech lay far to the north (near the Black Sea) and Kedar in the Arabian desert; the names stand for hostile, distant peoples.

chapters.title: A song for the ascents.

verses.text:
I lift my eyes to the mountains—
where does my help come from?

My help comes from Yahweh,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

He will not let your foot slip;
your guardian will not doze.

Look, he who guards Israel
neither dozes nor sleeps.

Yahweh is your guardian;
Yahweh is your shade at your right hand.

The sun will not harm you by day,
nor the moon at night.

Yahweh will guard you from all harm;
he will guard your life.

Yahweh will guard your going out and your coming in
from now on and forevermore.

chapters.title: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text:
I rejoiced when they said to me,
“Let us go to the house of Yahweh!”

Our feet have been standing
within your gates, Jerusalem—

Jerusalem, built as a city
bound firmly together,

For there the thrones for judgment stand,
the thrones of the house of David.

Ask for Jerusalem’s peace!{b}
“May all who love you live at ease!

May peace be within your ramparts,
security within your towers!”

For the sake of my kin and my companions
I will speak: “Within you be peace!”

For the sake of the house of Yahweh our God,
I will seek your good.

notes.text: Hebrew “a testimony for Israel.”
The Hebrew plays on the sounds of shalom (peace), Yerushalaim (Jerusalem), and shalvah (ease, security).

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
Toward you I raise my eyes,
you who sit enthroned in the heavens!

Look—as the eyes of servants are on the hand of their lord,
as the eyes of a maid are on the hand of her mistress,
so our eyes are on Yahweh our God,
until he shows us grace.

Be gracious to us, Yahweh, be gracious to us,
for we have had more than our fill of contempt.

Too long our soul has been sated
with the scorn of the complacent,
with the contempt of the arrogant.

chapters.title: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text:
“If it had not been Yahweh who was for us”—
let Israel now say—

“if it had not been Yahweh who was for us
when people rose up against us,

then they would have swallowed us alive
when their anger blazed against us;

then the flood would have carried us off;
the torrent would have rolled over our soul;

then over our soul
the raging waters would have gone.”

Blessed be Yahweh,
who has not handed us over as prey for their teeth!

Our soul has escaped like a bird
from the fowler’s snare;
the snare is broken,
and we have escaped!

Our help is in the name of Yahweh,
the Maker of heaven and earth.

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
Those who trust in Yahweh are like Mount Zion,
which cannot be shaken but stands forever.

As the mountains surround Jerusalem,
so Yahweh surrounds his people,
from now on and forevermore.

For the scepter of wickedness will not rest
on the land allotted to the righteous,
so that the righteous do not reach out their hands to do wrong.

Do good, Yahweh, to those who are good,
and to those who are upright in their hearts!

But those who turn aside to their crooked ways
Yahweh will lead away with the evildoers.
Peace be on Israel!

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
When Yahweh restored the fortunes of Zion,{a}
we were like those who dream.

Then our mouths were full of laughter,
our tongues of joyful singing.
Among the nations people said,
“Yahweh has done great things for them.”

Yahweh has done great things for us;
we are glad.

Restore our fortunes,{b} Yahweh,
like streams in the Negev!{c}

Those who sow in tears
will reap with shouts of joy.

He who goes out weeping,
carrying the seed for sowing,
will surely come home with shouts of joy,
carrying his sheaves.

notes.text: Or “brought back the captives of Zion.”
So the qere; the ketiv has a variant form of the same noun.
The dry south country, where seasonal streambeds suddenly run full after rain.

chapters.title: A song of ascents. Of Solomon.

verses.text:
Unless Yahweh builds the house,
its builders labor over it in vain.
Unless Yahweh guards the city,
the watchman stays awake in vain.

Look, children are a heritage from Yahweh,
the fruit of the womb a reward.

Like arrows in a warrior’s hand
are sons born in one’s youth.

Happy is the man
who has filled his quiver with them!
They will not be put to shame
when they speak with enemies in the gate.

notes.text: Or “he provides for his beloved while they sleep.” “Beloved” (yedid) echoes Jedidiah, a name of Solomon (2 Samuel 12:25).

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
Happy is everyone who fears Yahweh,
who walks in his ways!

You will eat the fruit of the labor of your hands;
you will be happy, and it will go well with you.

Your wife within your house
will be like a vine heavy with fruit;
around your table your children
will be like young olive trees.

Look, this is how the man will be blessed
who fears Yahweh.

Yahweh bless you out of Zion!
May you look on Jerusalem’s good
every day you live!

May you see your children’s children!
Peace be on Israel!

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
“Many times from my youth they have assailed me”—
let Israel now say—

“many times from my youth they have assailed me,
yet they have not overcome me.

Plowmen plowed across my back;
they made their furrows long.”{a}

Yahweh is righteous;
he has cut the cords of the wicked.

Let all who hate Zion
be put to shame and turned back!

Let them be like grass on the rooftops,
which dries up before it can be pulled up,

grass that fills no reaper’s hand,
no armful for one who binds sheaves,

nor do those who pass by say,
“The blessing of Yahweh be on you!
We bless you in the name of Yahweh!”

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has a variant spelling.

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text: Out of the depths I call to you, Yahweh!

Lord, hear my voice!
Let your ears be attentive
to the voice of my pleas for mercy!

If you, Yah, kept a record of iniquities,
Lord, who could stand?

But forgiveness is with you,
that you may be held in awe.

I wait for Yahweh; my whole soul waits,
and I put my hope in his word.

My soul waits for the Lord
more than watchmen for the morning,
more than watchmen for the morning.

Israel, hope in Yahweh!
For with Yahweh there is covenant love,
and with him is abundant redemption.

And he will redeem Israel
from all its iniquities.

chapters.title: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, there is no pride in my heart,
no haughtiness in my eyes;
I do not reach after great matters,
or things too wondrous for me.

Israel, hope in Yahweh
from now on and forevermore.

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
Remember, Yahweh, in David’s favor,
all the hardship he endured,

how he swore to Yahweh
and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:

“I will not enter the tent of my house
or get into my bed;

I will not give sleep to my eyes
or slumber to my eyelids,

until I find a place for Yahweh,
a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”

Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah;{a}
we found it in the fields of Jaar.{b}

“Let us enter where he dwells;
let us bow low at his footstool!”

Arise, Yahweh, and go to your resting place,
you and the ark of your might.

Let your priests be clothed with righteousness,
and let your faithful ones shout for joy.

For the sake of your servant David,
do not reject your anointed king.{c}

Yahweh swore to David in truth,
an oath he will not take back:
“From the fruit of your body
I will place one on your throne.

If your sons keep my covenant
and my testimonies that I will teach them,
their sons also forever
will sit on your throne.”

For Yahweh has chosen Zion;
he has desired it as his dwelling:

“Here is my resting place forevermore;
here I will make my home, for I have longed for it.

I will richly bless her provisions;
I will satisfy her poor with bread.

Her priests I will clothe with salvation,
and her faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.

There I will cause a horn to spring up for David;
I have set out a lamp for my anointed one.

I will dress his enemies in shame,
but on his head his crown will gleam.”

notes.text: Possibly the region of Bethlehem (Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:2), or of Kiriath-jearim.
“Forest,” probably Kiriath-jearim, where the ark stayed for twenty years (1 Samuel 7:1–2).
Verses 8–10 are closely paralleled in 2 Chronicles 6:41–42.

chapters.title: A song of ascents. Of David.

verses.text:
Look how good and how pleasant it is
when brothers live together in unity!

It is like the fine oil on the head,
flowing down on the beard,
on Aaron’s beard,
flowing down to the neck of his garments.

It is like the dew of Hermon
that falls on the mountains of Zion.
For there Yahweh has commanded the blessing:
life forevermore.

chapters.title: A song of ascents.

verses.text:
Come, bless Yahweh,
all you servants of Yahweh,
who stand by night in the house of Yahweh!

Lift up your hands toward the sanctuary
and bless Yahweh!

May Yahweh bless you from Zion,
he who made heaven and earth!

Hallelujah!
Praise the name of Yahweh!
Give praise, you servants of Yahweh,

you who stand in the house of Yahweh,
in the courts of the house of our God!

Praise Yah, for Yahweh is good;
sing to his name, for it is lovely!

For Yah has chosen Jacob for himself,
Israel as his treasured possession.

For I know that Yahweh is great,
and that our Lord is above all gods.

Whatever Yahweh pleases, he does,
in the heavens and on the earth,
in the seas and all the deeps.

He struck down the firstborn of Egypt,
of human and of beast alike.

Into your midst, Egypt, he sent signs and wonders,
on Pharaoh and on all who served him.

He struck down many nations
and killed mighty kings—

Sihon king of the Amorites,
Og king of Bashan,
and all the kingdoms of Canaan—

and he handed over their land as a heritage,
a heritage to Israel his people.

Yahweh, your name endures forever,
your renown, Yahweh, through all generations.

For Yahweh will vindicate his people
and have compassion on his servants.{a}

The idols of the nations are silver and gold,
the work of human hands.

Mouths they have, yet they cannot speak;
eyes they have, yet they cannot see;

ears they have, yet they cannot hear,
and no breath is in their mouths at all.

Their makers will grow like them,
and so will everyone who relies on them.{b}

House of Israel, bless Yahweh!
House of Aaron, bless Yahweh!

House of Levi, bless Yahweh!
You who fear Yahweh, bless Yahweh!

Blessed from Zion be Yahweh,
who dwells in Jerusalem!
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Verse 14 repeats Deuteronomy 32:36.
Verses 15–18 closely follow Psalm 115:4–8.

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good,
for his covenant love endures forever.{a}

Give thanks to the God of gods,
for his covenant love endures forever.

Give thanks to the Lord of lords,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who alone does great wonders,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who by understanding made the heavens,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who spread out the earth above the waters,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who made the great lights,
for his covenant love endures forever—

the sun to govern the day,
for his covenant love endures forever;

the moon and stars to rule over the night,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who struck Egypt through their firstborn,
for his covenant love endures forever,

and brought Israel out from among them,
for his covenant love endures forever,

with a strong hand and an outstretched arm,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who split the Red Sea in two,
for his covenant love endures forever,

and made Israel pass through the middle of it,
for his covenant love endures forever,

but shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who led his people through the wilderness,
for his covenant love endures forever;

to him who struck great kings,
for his covenant love endures forever,

and killed majestic kings,
for his covenant love endures forever—

Sihon king of the Amorites,
for his covenant love endures forever,

and Og king of Bashan,
for his covenant love endures forever—

and gave their land as an inheritance,
for his covenant love endures forever,

an inheritance for Israel his servant,
for his covenant love endures forever;

who remembered us when we were brought low,
for his covenant love endures forever,

and snatched us from our foes,
for his covenant love endures forever;

who gives food to all flesh,
for his covenant love endures forever.

Give thanks to the God of heaven,
for his covenant love endures forever.

notes.text: Every verse of this psalm ends with the same response, “for his covenant love endures forever” (ki leʿolam khasdo), apparently sung by the congregation in answer to a leader. Jewish tradition calls it “the Great Hallel.”

verses.text:
By the rivers of Babylon—
there we sat down and wept
when we remembered Zion.

On the poplars{a} there
we hung up our lyres.

There our captors
requested songs from us,
and those who mocked us wanted entertainment:
“Sing us a song from Zion!”

How could we sing a song of Yahweh
on foreign soil?

If I forget you, Jerusalem,
let my right hand forget its skill!

Let my tongue stick to my palate
if I do not remember you,
if I do not value Jerusalem
more than my greatest joy!

Remember, Yahweh, against the sons of Edom
the day of Jerusalem,
how they said, “Strip it bare, strip it bare,
down to its foundations!”

Daughter of Babylon, you destroyer soon destroyed,
happy is he who pays you back
the full measure you dealt to us!

Happy is he who takes hold of your little ones
and smashes them on the rock!{b}

notes.text: Traditionally “willows”; the tree is probably the Euphrates poplar.

The psalm ends with a raw cry for retribution from people who had seen their own children slaughtered (compare Isaiah 13:16; Hosea 13:16; Nahum 3:10). It voices the exiles’ anguish and hands vengeance over to God in prayer (compare Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19); it is not a command to be carried out. The CJT translates it without softening.

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
I give you thanks with all my heart;
before the gods{a} I sing your praise.

The day I called out, you answered me;
you emboldened me, putting strength in my soul.

All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, Yahweh,
when they have heard the words of your mouth,

and they will sing of the ways of Yahweh,
for great is the glory of Yahweh.

For though Yahweh is high, he looks on the lowly,
but the haughty he knows from far away.

Though I walk through the thick of trouble,
you preserve my life;
you put out your hand against my enemies’ rage,
and your right hand rescues me.

Yahweh will complete his purpose for me.
Yahweh, your covenant love endures forever.
Do not let go of the works of your hands!

notes.text: Hebrew ʾelohim; possibly the heavenly beings, or the gods of the nations (so many interpreters), or rulers. The Septuagint has “angels.”
The Hebrew is unusual; it may mean that God has exalted his word even beyond all that his name had revealed, or “you have exalted your name and your word above all things.”

chapters.title: To the choirmaster. Of David. A psalm.

verses.text: Yahweh, you have searched me and you know me.

Whether I sit or stand, you know it;
you perceive my thoughts from afar.

You measure out my journeys and my resting;
you know all my ways through and through.

Before there is a word on my tongue,
look, Yahweh, you know it completely.

You hem me in, behind and before;
you have laid your hand on me.

Such knowledge is too wonderful for me;{a}
it is too high—I cannot reach it.

Where could I go from your Spirit?
Where could I flee from your presence?

If I go up to the heavens, you are there;
if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there!

If I take the wings of the dawn
and settle at the far side of the sea,

even there your hand will lead me,
and your right hand will hold me fast.

If I say, “The darkness will surely hide me,
and the light around me will turn to night,”

For you formed my inward parts;{b}
you wove me together in my mother’s womb.

My frame was not hidden from you
when I was made in secret,
intricately woven in the depths of the earth.

How precious to me are your thoughts, God!
How vast is the sum of them!

If I tried to count them, they would outnumber the sand.
I wake up, and I am still with you.

If only you would slay the wicked, God!
Men of bloodshed, get away from me!

They speak of you with wicked intent;
your adversaries take your name in vain.{e}

Do I not hate those who hate you, Yahweh?
Do I not loathe those who rise up against you?

With perfect hatred I hate them;
they have become enemies to me.

Search me out, God, and know my heart!
Try me, and know my troubled thoughts!

See whether there is any hurtful way in me,
and lead me in the everlasting way!

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv has a variant form of the same word.
Hebrew “kidneys,” the seat of the deepest emotions.
The Hebrew is difficult; the Septuagint and some other ancient versions read “for you are awe-inspiring and wonderful.”
The final line follows the ketiv (lo, “not”). The qere reads lo, “to him / for it,” giving a sense such as “and for it there was one of them.” The verse is notoriously difficult.
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.

chapters.title: To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Rescue me, Yahweh, from evil men;
guard me from men of violence,

who scheme evil in their hearts
and every day stir up battles.

They make their tongues sharp as a snake’s;
the poison of vipers is behind their lips. Selah

I say to Yahweh, “You are my God.”
Give ear, Yahweh, to the voice of my pleas for mercy!

Yahweh, my Lord, the strength of my salvation,
you have shielded my head in the day of battle.

As for the heads of those who surround me,
let the trouble of their own lips cover them!

Let no slanderer find a footing in the land;
let disaster hunt the violent man down, blow upon blow!

I know{b} that Yahweh will uphold the cause of the afflicted
and justice for the needy.

Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name;
the upright will dwell in your presence.

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv may be read “let him bring down burning coals on them.”
So the qere; the ketiv reads “you know.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, I call to you; hurry to me!
Give ear to my voice when I call to you!

May my prayer rise before you like incense,
my raised hands like the evening sacrifice.

Set a guard, Yahweh, over my mouth;
keep watch over the door of my lips!

Do not let my heart incline to anything evil,
to busy myself with wicked deeds
alongside men who do wrong,
and let me not eat of their delicacies!

When their judges are thrown down from the sides of the cliff,
then they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.

As when one plows and breaks up the ground,
so our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

But my eyes are toward you, Yahweh, my Lord;
in you I take refuge; do not pour out my life!

Keep me from the trap they have laid for me
and from the snares of evildoers!

Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
while I pass by in safety.

notes.text: Verses 5–7 are among the most obscure in the Psalter; the translation is tentative.

chapters.title: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave.{a} A prayer.

verses.text:
With my voice I cry out to Yahweh;
with my voice I plead with Yahweh for mercy.

I pour out my complaint before him;
I tell my trouble before him.

When my spirit grows faint within me,
you are the one who knows my path!
On the path where I walk
they have hidden a trap for me.

Pay attention to my cry,
for I am brought very low!
Rescue me from my pursuers,
for they are too strong for me!

Lead me out of prison
so that I can praise your name!
The righteous will surround me
because you will be good to me.

notes.text: Compare 1 Samuel 22:1; 24:3; and the title of Psalm 57.

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Do not put your servant on trial,
for no one alive is righteous in your sight.

And so my spirit fails within me;
my heart is stunned inside me.

I spread out my hands to you;
my soul thirsts for you like a parched land. Selah

Make haste to answer me, Yahweh!
My spirit is spent!
Do not turn your face away,
or I will be like those who sink into the pit.

In the morning let me hear of your covenant love,
for my trust is in you.
Show me the road to walk on,
for to you I raise my soul.

Deliver me from my enemies, Yahweh!
With you I have taken shelter.{a}

Teach me to carry out your will,
for you are my God!
May your good Spirit guide me
on even ground!

For your name’s sake, Yahweh, keep me alive!
In your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble!

And in your covenant love cut off my enemies,
and destroy all the adversaries of my soul,
for I am your servant.

notes.text: The Hebrew is uncertain; the Septuagint has “to you I have fled.”

chapters.title: Of David.

verses.text:
my covenant love{a} and my fortress,
my stronghold and my deliverer,
my shield, in whom I take refuge,
who subdues my people{b} under me.

Yahweh, what is man that you take note of him,
the son of man that you give him a thought?

Man is like a breath;
his days are like a passing shadow.

Yahweh, bend your heavens and come down!
Touch the mountains so that they smoke!

Flash out lightning and scatter them;
send your arrows and rout them!

whose mouths speak falsehood
and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.

God, I will sing a new song to you;
on a ten-stringed harp I will make music to you,

to him who gives victory to kings,
who sets David his servant free from the cruel sword.

Set me free and rescue me
from the hand of foreigners,
whose mouths speak falsehood
and whose right hand is a right hand of lies.

May our sons in their youth
be like plants grown tall,
our daughters like corner pillars
carved for the building of a palace;

Happy is the people for whom it is so!
Happy is the people whose God is Yahweh!

notes.text: Hebrew khasdi, “my covenant love”—that is, the God who shows me covenant love. Psalm 18:2 and 2 Samuel 22 have “my rock.”
Many Hebrew manuscripts, the Aramaic, and Syriac read “peoples” (compare Psalm 18:47; 2 Samuel 22:48).
Or “may our chieftains be firmly established.” The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.

chapters.title: A song of praise. Of David.{a}

verses.text:
I will lift you up, my God and King,
and praise your name forever and ever.

Each day I will bless you
and give praise to your name for all time and beyond.

Great is Yahweh and most worthy of praise;
his greatness is beyond searching out.

One generation will commend your works to the next
and tell of your mighty acts.

I will ponder the glorious splendor of your majesty
and the record of your wonders.{b}

They will speak of the power of your awesome deeds,
and I will declare your greatness.{c}

They will pour out the memory of your abundant goodness
and sing joyfully of your righteousness.

Gracious and compassionate is Yahweh,
slow to anger and great in covenant love.

Yahweh is good toward everyone;
his mercy rests on all his works.

All your works will give you thanks, Yahweh,
and your faithful ones will bless you.

They will speak of the glory of your kingdom
and tell of your might,

to make known to the children of men his mighty acts
and the glorious splendor of his kingdom.

Your kingdom lasts through all the ages,
and your rule continues in every generation.
[God is faithful in everything he says
and kind in everything he does.]{d}

Yahweh holds up all who are falling
and raises up all who are bowed down.

All eyes wait on you,
and you give them their food when it is due.

You open your hand
and satisfy the desire of every living thing.

Yahweh is righteous in all his ways
and faithful in all his works.

Yahweh is near to all who call on him,
to all who call on him in truth.

He grants what those who fear him long for;
he listens to their cry and rescues them.

Yahweh watches over all who love him,
but all the wicked he will destroy.

My mouth will speak the praise of Yahweh,
and let all flesh bless his holy name
forever and ever.

notes.text: Psalm 145 is an alphabetic acrostic: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In the standard Hebrew text the nun (נ) line, which should come between verses 13 and 14, is missing. A nun line is found in the Psalms Scroll from Qumran (11QPs-a), in the Septuagint and Syriac, and in one medieval Masoretic manuscript. The CJT includes it in brackets at the end of verse 13. Psalms 9–10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, and 119 are also acrostics. In 11QPs-a, each verse of this psalm is followed by the refrain “Blessed be Yahweh and blessed be his name forever and ever.” This is the only psalm titled tehillah, “song of praise,” the word from which the Hebrew name of the whole book, Tehillim, comes.
The Septuagint and 11QPs-a read “They will speak of the glorious splendor of your majesty, and tell of your wondrous works.”
So the qere; the ketiv reads “your great deeds.”

The bracketed nun line (Hebrew neʾeman, “faithful”) is not in the standard Masoretic Text. It is attested in 11QPs-a (which reads “God”), the Septuagint (which reads “the Lord,” suggesting Hebrew YHWH), the Syriac, and one Masoretic manuscript. Compare verse 17, which it closely resembles. The CJT includes it because it completes the acrostic and has early, independent support; readers may treat it as a probable but uncertain part of the text.

verses.text:
Hallelujah!{a}
Praise Yahweh, my soul!

I will praise Yahweh as long as I live;
I will sing to my God while I have my being.

Do not put your trust in princes,
in a son of man, who cannot save.

His breath departs; he returns to his ground;
on that very day his plans perish.

Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help,
who rests his hope on Yahweh his God,

Yahweh will reign forever,
your God, Zion, for all generations.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Psalms 146–150, the closing “Hallel” of the Psalter, each begin and end with “Hallelujah” (“Praise Yah!”).

verses.text:
Yahweh builds up Jerusalem;
he gathers the outcasts of Israel.

He heals the brokenhearted
and binds up their wounds.

He counts out the number of the stars;
he calls each of them by name.

Our Lord is great and enormously powerful;
his understanding cannot be measured.

Yahweh raises up the lowly;
he throws the wicked to the ground.

Sing to Yahweh with thanksgiving;
make music to our God on the lyre!

He gives the animals their food,
and the young ravens when they call.

He takes no delight in the strength of the horse,
nor pleasure in the legs of a man;

Yahweh takes pleasure in those who fear him,
in those who hope in his covenant love.

Praise Yahweh, Jerusalem!
Praise your God, Zion!

For he has made firm the bars of your gates;
he has blessed your sons within you.

He makes peace within your borders;
he satisfies you with the finest wheat.

He dispatches his command to the earth;
his word races along.

He spreads out snow like wool;
he strews the frost like ash.

He hurls down his hail like crumbs;
who can stand before his cold?

He sends his word and they melt;
he stirs his wind, and the waters run.

He declares his word{b} to Jacob,
his statutes and rules to Israel.

notes.text: The Septuagint divides this psalm into two: verses 1–11 are its Psalm 146, and verses 12–20 its Psalm 147. From here on the Greek and Latin numbering again matches the Hebrew (see the note on the numbering of the Psalms at Psalm 1).
So the qere; the ketiv reads “his words.”

verses.text:
Praise him, all his angels;
praise him, all his host!{a}

Praise him, sun and moon;
praise him, all you shining stars!

Praise him, you heaven of heavens,
you waters that are above the skies!

Let them praise the name of Yahweh,
for he commanded and they were created.

He set them in place forever and ever;
he fixed a limit that will not be passed.

Praise Yahweh from the earth,
you sea monsters and all deeps,

Fire and hail, snow and fog,
storm wind that does what he says!

Mountains and all hills,
fruit trees and all cedars!

Wild animals and all livestock,
creeping things and flying birds!

Kings of the earth and all peoples,
princes and all rulers of the earth!

Young men and young women alike,
old and young together!

He has lifted high a horn for his people,
a cause of praise for all his faithful ones,
for the children of Israel, a people close to him.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: So the qere; the ketiv reads “hosts.”

verses.text:
Hallelujah!
Sing to Yahweh a new song,
his praise in the assembly of the faithful!

Let Israel rejoice in his Maker;
let the children of Zion delight in their King!

Let them praise his name with dancing,
making music to him with tambourine and lyre!

For Yahweh takes pleasure in his people;
he crowns the humble with salvation.

Let the faithful exult in glory;
let them sing for joy on their beds.

Let praises to God be in their mouths
and a double-edged sword in their hands,

to carry out vengeance on the nations
and punishment on the peoples,

to bind their kings with chains
and their nobles with fetters of iron,

to carry out on them the judgment written!
This is the honor of all his faithful ones.
Hallelujah!

Praise him for his mighty deeds;
praise him for his surpassing greatness!

Praise him with the sounding of the horn;
praise him with lute and lyre!

Praise him with tambourine and dancing;
praise him with strings and flute!

Praise him with clashing cymbals;
praise him with resounding cymbals!

Let everything that has breath praise Yah!
Hallelujah!{b}

notes.text: Psalm 150 is the closing doxology of Book Five and of the whole Psalter. Each of the first four books ends with a short blessing (41:13; 72:18–19; 89:52; 106:48); the fifth ends with an entire psalm of praise, in which “praise” (hallelu) sounds thirteen times.

The Psalms Scroll from Qumran (11QPs-a, first century AD) contains many of the psalms of Books Four and Five, but in an order that differs considerably from the Masoretic Text, mixed with other compositions (among them a “Plea for Deliverance,” an “Apostrophe to Zion,” a “Hymn to the Creator,” and a prose note crediting David with 4,050 songs). Scholars debate whether it is a liturgical collection or evidence that the order of the last third of the Psalter was still fluid. The CJT follows the Masoretic order. Near its end the scroll also has a Hebrew form of Psalm 151, which the Septuagint includes as a short autobiographical psalm of David “outside the number” of the 150; it will be translated in the CJT’s Apocrypha.
